output: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany criticizes the Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, asserting they protect established clubs rather than preventing teams from going bankrupt. City, who have a £49m transfer budget this season due to FFP breaches, were fined £50 million last year. Kompany believes FFP prevents other teams from challenging the upper echelons of football, and claims City's success is due to their owners' investment, which has improved the community and the city of Manchester.

Bath rugby club has signed England Sevens international Jeff Williams for the upcoming season. The 26-year-old, who has previously played for South Africa and France, has 36 tries on the World Series circuit and recently helped England win the Tokyo Sevens. Williams, who is English through his father, will bring a high-tempo, dynamic style of play to Bath, in line with the club's attacking ethos.

Jared Leto has been cast as the Joker in the 2016 film "Suicide Squad," marking his first appearance as the character on the big screen since Heath Ledger. The film, which does not feature Batman, also stars Will Smith, Margot Robbie, and a variety of other villains and anti-heroes. "Suicide Squad" is set to release in theaters on August 5, 2016.

Three Florida corrections officers and a trainee have been charged with conspiring to murder a former inmate, according to the Florida Attorney General's office. An undercover FBI operation led to the arrests, with the men being active members of a local KKK faction. They were led to believe they had successfully carried out the murder through a staged crime scene and photos. Each man faces up to 30 years in prison if convicted. Florida Attorney General Pam Bondi stated that such hate-fueled violence would not be tolerated.

The conference call for Manny Pacquiao's media event discussing his upcoming fight with Floyd Mayweather was abruptly cancelled due to technical difficulties caused by a high number of boxing writers and broadcasters joining the call. Pacquiao managed to answer only one question before the call was cancelled. The call has been rescheduled due to the technical issues, while Mayweather is due to address the media in a conference call on Wednesday.

1. Serena Williams celebrated her 700th career victory and advancement to the Miami Open semi-finals with a giant cake, while Andy Murray was also honored with a cake for his 500th career win.

2. In the subsequent match, Williams outplayed Sabine Lisicki 7-6, 1-6, 6-3, avenging a past Wimbledon defeat, but her elder sister Venus was eliminated by Carla Suarez Navarro.

3. Simona Halep achieved victory over Sloane Stephens, guaranteeing a spot in the semi-finals against Williams, offering the possibility of a Williams sister duel if Venus can overcome Suarez Navarro in their next match.

The world's largest terminal, Terminal 1 at Beijing International Airport (also known as Daxing Airport), is set to open in 2018, aiming to accommodate the significant rise in Chinese tourists traveling globally. Designed by Zaha Hadid and ADPI, the terminal will offer a spacious and open layout with a flowing roof design and a central multi-layered courtyard. The project, which will cover 700,000 square meters and handle 45 million passengers annually, is a response to the increasing number of Chinese tourists, who, as per a 2014 study by Bank of America Merrill Lynch, totaled 109 million and spent $164 billion.

Manchester United's manager, Louis van Gaal, confirmed that Wayne Rooney sustained a knee injury during the Premier League match against Everton. Rooney was replaced by Robin van Persie in the 88th minute of the game, which ended in a 3-0 loss for United. The severity of the injury is yet to be determined, with Van Gaal stating they will have to wait and see. The defeat, which was United's first back-to-back losses in the league since Van Gaal took over, has potentially opened the door for Liverpool to challenge for fourth place in the league standings.

Jack Wilshere, an Arsenal midfielder, was shopping for his groceries, a common activity for footballers during transfer periods. Despite being sidelined with an ankle injury, he is at the brink of full recovery. The contents of his trolley, posted on his Instagram, included Seriously Fruity Mixed Berry Crisp, Oats and Honey Special K, eggs, baked beans, and corn on the cob, suggesting a healthy and protein-rich diet. The shopping excursion left Wilshere tired, as evident in his Instagram post asking for help from his followers to put away the groceries.

A Venezuelan woman, Marleni Olivo, threw a mango with her phone number on it at President Nicolas Maduro, who was riding a bus, in a bid to address her housing issues. To her surprise, Maduro mentioned the incident during his live TV broadcast, offering her a new apartment as a solution to her problem. Critics have labeled the event as a "manguicidio," a play on words meaning assassination of a powerful leader, but Olivo claimed she had no malicious intent and was simply trying to solve her housing problems.

Carlos Tevez, a former Manchester United and City striker currently playing for Juventus in Serie A, believes it is harder to score goals in Italy than in the Premier League. He credits this to the style of play, particularly the midfield, and the increased number of defenders faced by strikers in the Italian league. Despite this challenge, he remains optimistic about Juventus' chances of winning the Champions League, citing the improved team dynamic compared to his previous experiences in England. Tevez won the Champion's League with Manchester United in 2008 and has scored 36 goals in Serie A since joining Juventus in 2013.

In the Premier League match between Manchester City and Crystal Palace, Yaya Toure was criticized by pundit Jamie Carragher for allegedly ducking out of the way during a free-kick that resulted in the match-winning goal. Carragher felt Toure's lack of effort in the five-man wall was unacceptable, and the incident left Manchester City nine points behind leaders Chelsea.

A 50-year-old Australian man died unexpectedly on April 29 while on holiday in Kuta, Bali. The incident occurred at the Rooftop Restaurant on the 101 Legian Hotel, where he was staying. Witnesses claim he had mentioned he wasn't feeling well shortly before collapsing, and a doctor at the scene suspects heart attack. The exact cause of death is yet to be determined through an autopsy, but initial observations suggest heart attack. Kuta, a popular Australian tourist destination, is known internationally for its long sandy beach and tourist development.

Richie Benaud, a former Australia cricket captain and well-known commentator, passed away last week at the age of 84 from complications of skin cancer. A private funeral service was held in Sydney on Wednesday for Benaud, attended by close family and friends. His family described him as a special person who meant a lot to them. Benaud was renowned for his commentary work in cricket, having worked for the BBC and Australian broadcasters for decades. After Benaud's death, numerous tributes were paid to him by cricket teams, players, and fans around the world.

A 16-year-old girl named Isobel Attwood has been missing for two days. She is believed to be with a man in his 20s, potentially in the Winchester or Southampton areas. Friends on social media claim she is safe but needs space, and police are appealing for help to find her, expressing concern for her welfare.

Manchester City players, including Sergio Aguero, David Silva, Joe Hart, and Yaya Toure, stand to lose £500,000 each in bonuses if they do not qualify for the Champions League this season. The Premier League champions have incentivized contracts to meet financial fair play requirements but are currently in fourth place, and a four-point gap from Liverpool, with their European qualification still uncertain. City's poor performance, including early exits in the FA Cup and Champions League, has led manager Manuel Pellegrini to express concern about the team's disintegration and the need for improvement. The team faces tough upcoming matches against West Ham United, Aston Villa, Tottenham Hotspur, Queens Park Rangers, Swansea City, and Southampton. The top three teams in the Premier League automatically qualify for the Champions League, with the fourth-place team needing to win a qualifying round to enter. Meanwhile, Manchester United, led by Louis van Gaal, are confident of securing top-class talent in the next transfer window, potentially including Juventus midfielder Paul Pogba.

Martin Skrtel, the Liverpool defender, has publicly denied rumors linking him to a move away from the club, with potential destinations being Wolfsburg and Napoli. Skrtel, at 30 years old and with over 200 league appearances for Liverpool, is expected to finalize a contract extension instead, as reported by his agent Karol Csonto. Liverpool, who have had a disappointing season, are anticipating a summer clear-out, but Skrtel is not among those expected to leave.

A CEO from Texas, Cheryl Rios, has faced criticism for stating that a woman cannot be president due to the 'hormones' that would supposedly hinder her from starting a war. She made the comments on Facebook following Hillary Clinton's announcement of her presidential candidacy. Despite the backlash, Rios maintains her opinions, stating that she supports women's rights but holds traditional beliefs about the presidency being a male position, referencing biblical reasoning but not citing a specific verse. The controversy has resulted in accusations of misogyny and hypocrisy on social media. In response, Rios has defended her opinions as valid and asked for an end to the negativity. She also clarified that she acknowledges the abilities of women in other fields such as law and medicine, but not the presidency.

1. Atletico Madrid striker Mario Mandzukic was injured during a physical Champions League quarter-final match against Real Madrid, suffering a cut to the nose from an elbow by Sergio Ramos and a punch to the stomach by Dani Carvajal. Despite his injuries, Mandzukic is expected to play in the second leg at the Bernabeu on Wednesday.
2. The first leg of the match ended in a 0-0 draw, with numerous fouls and fights dominating the second half.
3. Mandzukic, who missed Atletico's La Liga match against Deportivo La Coruna due to an ankle injury, is currently back in training and is favored to play in the second leg of the Champions League quarter-final alongside Antoine Griezmann who has been in excellent form for the team.

Jose Mourinho mistakenly believed Marouane Fellaini would play against Chelsea due to a misunderstanding with a hotel doorman who was giving tickets to Fellaini's twin brother Mansour. Mourinho had prepared Chelsea's Kurt Zouma to mark Fellaini, with Ruben Loftus-Cheek practicing against him in training. In reality, Fellaini did play in the match at Stamford Bridge, where Chelsea won 1-0, putting them on the verge of the Premier League title.

A woman identified as Dawn Milosky from Beachwood, New Jersey, was rescued from an overturned, burning vehicle in Kinnelon. Police arrived at the scene after receiving a tip-off about erratic driving. The woman, initially unconscious, was quickly freed from the wreckage and administered CPR. She was charged with DWI, having an open container, reckless driving, and failure to stay in the right lane. Milosky was airlifted to Morristown Medical Center but is reported to be doing okay now. The vehicle ignited 2 minutes and 30 seconds after she was removed from it.

A Chinese farmer at his goat farm in Chaohu, Anhui Province, recently discovered a six-legged kid among his herd. The animal, born 20 days ago and affectionately named the 'spider goat', boasts four forelegs and two hind legs and has become the country's latest curiosity. Despite initial doubts about the creature's survival, it is thriving with an 'extraordinary' appetite, making it one of the most playful additions to the farm. The farmer has chosen not to remove the two extra legs, opting for natural growth under his care.

West Ham United is reportedly interested in signing Javier Hernandez from Real Madrid this summer, as the Mexican striker, who scored a crucial goal against Atletico Madrid, is out of favor at Real under coach Carlo Ancelotti. Hernandez has one year left on his contract at Manchester United, where he currently resides but is not a part of Louis van Gaal's plans, potentially making him available for around £7 million. West Ham is focusing on young transfer targets for their final season at Upton Park, with implications towards Pedro Obiang, Moussa Konate, and Fabian Schar at the forefront of their recruitment plans.

1. Manager Stuart McCall of Rangers has dismissed any discussions about his future before the end of the season, emphasizing that his current revival of the club has yet to achieve anything significant, despite three consecutive wins.
2. McCall has restored a positive atmosphere at the club, which has been endorsed by the supporters, and he is focused solely on the team's upcoming match against Queen of the South.
3. The former Motherwell boss has expressed that his priority is winning matches, and he expects no meaningful talks with the Rangers board regarding his future until after the play-offs. McCall is also cautiously optimistic about the imminent arrival of Shane Ferguson on loan from Newcastle, who is recovering from a long-term knee injury.

Werder Bremen secured a 1-0 win against Hamburg SV, thanks to Franco Di Santo's 84th-minute penalty, keeping Bremen in contention for a Europa League spot. Hamburg's Valon Behrami was sent off at the penalty spot, and new coach Bruno Labbadia suffered a loss in his return to Hamburg's bench. The defeat left Hamburg in last place, while Bremen moved up to seventh in the Bundesliga standings. Meanwhile, second-placed VfL Wolfsburg aims to reduce Bayern Munich's lead to 10 points with their match against Schalke 04 later on Sunday, following Bayern's 2-0 victory over Hoffenheim on Saturday. Bayer Leverkusen is currently third after their 4-0 victory over Hanover 96.

A two-year-old boy fell approximately 10-12 feet into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after his parents dangled him over the edge. The child, who sustained minor injuries, was rescued by his parents before emergency responders arrived. The cheetahs did not approach the parents or the child during the incident. The zoo plans to press child endangerment charges against the family.

A Russian TV channel rated Hillary Clinton's first campaign video as Mature due to fears it might contravene the country's anti-gay propaganda law. The two-second clip of a gay couple holding hands is considered potentially offensive by the law, which bars public discussion of gay rights and relationships within earshot of children. This law drew criticism from international organizations, politicians, and activists after its passage in 2013, with some calling for boycotts and protests.

Siem de Jong, Newcastle United's Dutch midfielder, played the first half in a comeback game with Newcastle Under 21s after a collapsed lung, but left at halftime due to the match ending in a 2-0 loss. De Jong had made only one Premier League start since joining from Ajax last summer. Originally expected to miss the rest of the season, he now has a minor chance to play in the last six matches, although his subdued performance suggests he might not recover in time for the visit of Tottenham. Derby County won their game against Newcastle, scoring second-half goals from Alefe Santos and Farrend Rawson.

Chef Ally Lees of Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham has created a three-foot, 12,000-calorie omelette using 150 eggs, containing an excessive 945g of protein, which exceeds the recommended daily amount for a man by 16 times. The colossal dish, which is too much for one person to eat, is designed to be shared among at least five individuals due to its size and protein content. The cooking process took Ally an hour with the help of a massive paella pan.

Three Olympic gold medalists, Jessica Ennis-Hill (heptathlon), Mo Farah (10,000 meters), and Greg Rutherford (long jump), will participate in the Sainsbury’s Anniversary Games in London this summer. Ennis-Hill, a national hero from the London 2012 Olympics, will make her first appearance since giving birth last summer. The three-day event, including a two-day Diamond League meeting and the Sainsbury’s IPC Athletics Grand Prix Final, aims to recreate the atmosphere of the 2013 Anniversary Games with sold-out crowds. Tickets are now available for purchase on britishathletics.org.uk.

A snack bar in Rio de Janeiro was found to use dog meat in their pastry fillings, after police discovered frozen dog carcasses in the establishment. The owner, Chinese Van Ruilonc, admitted to using stray dogs he had collected from the city's streets as the meat source for his pastries. Additionally, police found evidence of workers being held against their will and forced to work for 18 hours a day without pay in a cage-like cell within the snack bar. Public prosecutor Guadalupe Louro Couto, who investigated the case, expressed shock at the discoveries and commented on the deplorable conditions.

The article details an incident where Ebony Dickens, using the pseudonym Tiffany Milan on Facebook, posted a threatening rant against white police officers, advocating for violence. The post included specific details about intended victims and a timeline for the attacks. The police in East Point, Georgia, along with the Atlanta police department, the FBI, and federal Homeland Security traced the post back to Dickens and arrested her; a firearm and three computers were found during the search of her residence. Dickens was charged with disseminating information related to terrorist acts, and a judge set a $10,000 bond for her, also banning her from social media.

PSV Eindhoven celebrated their first Dutch championship victory in seven years by beating Heerenveen 4-1, securing 79 points and surpassing Ajax Amsterdam's total. Striker Luuk de Jong scored two first-half goals, Memphis Depay added a stunning free-kick, and Luciano Narsingh and Derrick Luckassen scored late on. At the bottom of the table, Dordrecht moved closer to relegation after a 3-0 loss at Vitesse Arnhem, while AZ Alkmaar secured a spot in the Europa League playoffs with a 3-1 home win over ADO Den Haag.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva was beaten to death by the head teacher of a school in Railamau village, India, allegedly for stealing a pencil and eraser. The teacher, Lalit Verma, has been arrested for culpable homicide not amounting to murder. This incident is said to be the latest in a series of reported cases of teachers physically abusing students in India, with similar incidents occurring in Burdwan, West Bengal, and Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh.

A gastrointestinal illness has affected approximately 100 passengers and crew members on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship, with symptoms including vomiting and diarrhea. The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) is currently investigating the cause of the illness, and two CDC staffers are scheduled to meet the ship in San Diego on Monday. Notably, this is the third time the Celebrity Infinity has experienced an outbreak of gastrointestinal illness, with previous incidents occurring in 2006 and 2013.

The article discusses a video of a Boston Terrier named Gizmo performing a unique trick, paw-stand walking, which involves standing on two feet and vertically launching his back legs in the air. This unusual stunt was captured on video by owner Loren Mathieson at home, with Gizmo attempting the trick while wearing new black boots. The video has attracted over 80,000 views and evoked laughter and delight from viewers. It is suggested that the performance was at first a response to the confusion Gizmo experienced when wearing the boots.

New Orleans has implemented a smoking ban in most locations, including bars, casinos, and restaurants, following a unanimous vote by the city council in January. This decision aims to protect workers from second-hand smoke. Some bar owners and patrons expressed concerns about potential revenue loss and the loss of smoking spots, leading to a lawsuit being filed to challenge the ban. The ban came into effect on the 1st of February, and violations will incur fines starting at $50. Notably, this change will not affect popular tourist attractions such as visiting Treme or eating beignets.

Manchester United Under-21, captained by Adnan Januzaj, secured a comeback victory against West Ham United in the Under-21 Premier League, going four points clear at the top. The game started with West Ham taking a surprising early lead through Reece Oxford, but the Red Devils responded quickly, with Josh Harrop scoring twice and Joe Rothwell adding another to complete an impressive turnaround. Despite dominance for most of the match, Manchester United struggled to extend their lead, with Jordan Brown equalizing just before half-time. Overall, Harrop's second goal secured a hard-earned victory for United.

Brisbane's Anglican Archbishop, Phillip Aspinall, has joined Catholic priest Paul Kelly in advocating for Queensland's controversial 'gay panic' homicide defense to be abolished. Aspinall believes that killing someone who sexually advances should not result in a reduced murder charge, and he encourages resistance against resorting to violence. Additionally, during his Easter Sunday mass, Aspinall appealed to those involved in anti-Islam rallies and church vandalism incidents in Melbourne to resist reacting out of fear.

Sandra Bullock, aged 50, has been named the world's most beautiful woman of 2015 by People magazine. She humorously labels the accolade as "ridiculous" and emphasizes the value of inner qualities such as kindness, good parenting, and laughter over physical appearance. The cover story features Bullock's home life with her son, Louis, 5, and her personal efforts to maintain health and fitness beyond her 40s. The selection of Bullock, the oldest woman to receive this title, has sparked discussions regarding age and beauty, with some praising it as a sign that beauty knows no age. Other prominent figures recognized in the "most beautiful" category this year include Gabrielle Union, Ariana Grande, and Laverne Cox. The issue will be available on newsstands from Friday.

On Monday morning, an improvised bomb exploded near a U.N. vehicle in Garowe, northeastern Somalia, killing six people, including four aid workers from UNICEF. The bomber, later identified as a member of the terrorist group Al-Shabaab, also died in the attack. In a separate incident on Sunday, three African Union troops were killed in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region of Somalia. This marks a continued series of violent attacks against the U.N., aid workers, and peacekeeping forces in Somalia.

A Texas wildlife park operator named Gary Saurage, resembling a modern-day Crocodile Dundee due to his baseball cap, was called to capture a massive 400-pound, 11-foot-long alligator residing in a family's backyard pond. In the capture, Saurage is seen approaching the aggressive beast with his bare hands and looking directly into its eyes. The alligator, later identified as a 35-to-40-year-old male, was eventually removed from the pond with assistance from others and returned to Saurage's wildlife park. Despite the impressive size, this particular capture wasn't a record for Saurage, as the largest alligator at his park, nicknamed Kong, measures 12 feet and 6 inches.

In eastern Turkey, five members of the Kurdistan Workers' Party were killed, and another was wounded in clashes with Turkish armed forces. Four Turkish soldiers were also wounded in the fighting, which occurred in the city of Agri. Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan condemned the violence, with Erdogan describing it as an attempt by Kurdish separatists to intervene in peace talks. Abdullah Ocalan, the leader of the Kurdistan Workers' Party, recently called for an end to violence from his prison cell, urging his followers to lay down their arms and focus on future negotiations. The ongoing conflict, which has lasted more than three decades, has resulted in the loss of approximately 40,000 lives and is often characterized as either a fight for Kurdish independence or a campaign of guerrilla war and terrorist acts. The Kurdish minority, making up about a fifth of Turkey's population, has historically faced cultural oppression, with many living in the underdeveloped southeastern part of Turkey.

Two 18-month-old twins tragically died after accidentally falling into a canal in Yuma, Arizona, on Friday morning. The area where the canal is located is commonly used by families for walks and jogging. Investigators are probing the incident but do not suspect foul play. The boys were rescued after an hour-long search, flown by a U.S. Marine Corps helicopter to a hospital, but were unfortunately pronounced dead.

Orlando City, an MLS team with a significant Latin-American fanbase coached by Adrian Heath, has shown interest in signing Manchester United's Javier Hernandez, who is currently on loan at Real Madrid. Hernandez, a Mexican international, could be a commercial boost for Orlando. Eight European clubs, including Southampton, Stoke, West Ham, Everton, Wolfsburg, AC Milan, Lazio, and Inter Milan, are also keen on the striker. Separately, Manchester United have made a revised contract offer to teenager Andreas Pereira, who has attracted interest from several European clubs, including Paris St Germain, Juventus, PSV Eindhoven, and Feyenoord, should he not agree to stay at United.

Couple Joel Burger and Ashley King, both 24, got engaged, with Ashley accepting the proposal. Known as "Burger King" since fifth grade due to the pair's names, they plan a unique wedding by serving drinks in personalized Burger King cups at their event, subject to approval from the international fast-food chain. They are long-term sweethearts who have embraced their playful nickname despite ongoing teasing from friends.

A 1960s hit band, unnamed in the article, was identified in a 1964 police intelligence report as attending a pedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London, the same location frequent by the deceased BBC star Jimmy Savile who was known to visit the brothel in the 1970s. It is not clear whether the band and Savile attended the brothel at the same time. In 2013, the senior officer in charge of Operation Yewtree, Detective Superintendent David Grey, began investigating the brothel following another police report mentioning it. The investigation revealed that a woman had come forward in 2003 claiming Savile had abused her during the 1970s following an appearance on Top of the Pops, but the details of the alleged assault were never put on the police computer. Det Supt Grey stated that while both the band and Savile were known to frequent the brothel, there was no evidence of a link between them at the time.

A German Shepherd named Sadie, from Alberta, Canada, was filmed playing an electric keyboard, using her paws to press keys and her nose to turn it on. Despite playing a minimalist, non-traditional piece with some off-key notes, Sadie's performance was well-received by viewers who found it adorable. Sadly, Sadie was rescued in 2009 and now enjoys learning new tricks, including playing the piano.

A man named Ivan Balashov, while browsing smartphones in a store in Novokuznetsk, Russia, took a selfie using one phone but preferred another. He attempted to leave the store with the second phone but was caught by shop security, claiming he wanted to buy it. However, he was later identified by police from the selfie, having it on the phone he initially used. Upon investigating, police traced him to his home where he denied involvement. Eventually, they were able to prove he had been at the store recently and found him guilty. He received a three-month suspended sentence for the phone theft.

The first trailer for the documentary "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name" has been released, showcasing the life and music of Amy Winehouse who struggled with drugs and alcohol during her career. In the trailer, Winehouse expresses ambivalence about fame, stating she doesn't think she could handle it. The documentary, endorsed by Winehouse's family, promises extensive unseen archive footage and previously unheard tracks. The film, directed by Asif Kapadia, has a UK release date set for July 3, with a US release date yet to be announced.

1. "The Big Bang Theory" features the return of Christine Baranski and Laurie Metcalf as the mothers of two characters, promised to be a standout episode.
2. Saturday Night Live, hosted by Scarlett Johansson, airs on NBC following the release of her new blockbuster Avengers movie.
3. Allison Janney delivers Emmy-worthy performances in the underrated Chuck Lorre dramedy "Mom," with the season finale airing this week.
4. The Rainn Wilson crime drama "Backstrom" concludes its season on Fox, with uncertainty about a potential fall return.
5. The dramatic series "Blue Bloods" with Tom Selleck concludes its two-part season finale, though its future remains in question.
6. The charming comedy "Younger," created by the creator of Sex and the City, has been renewed for a second season, making it a good time to start or continue watching the series starring Sutton Foster and Hilary Duff.

1. Fans of Downton Abbey may still see the character Violet, Countess of Grantham, played by Dame Maggie Smith, as she is rumored to appear in a new series created by Julian Fellowes, called The Gilded Age, set in New York during the late 19th Century.
2. The new series, The Gilded Age, is being produced by NBC and will focus on wealthy figures such as Cornelius Vanderbilt and John Jacob Astor, with Violet reappearing as her younger self.
3. Other characters like Robert, the Earl of Grantham, and his wife Cora, who is American-born, may also make appearances, but plans for the series are still in development, with filming potentially starting after Fellowes finishes Downton Abbey.

Steven Gerrard, who is concluding his career with Liverpool, has been selected to play in the FA Cup semi-final against Aston Villa at Wembley. This will be his 36th and potentially final game at the stadium. Despite a recent three-match ban, Gerrard is returning to the side following his impressive performance in a behind-closed-doors game, as praised by manager Brendan Rodgers. Throughout his career, Gerrard has demonstrated his significant impact in crucial matches, including his first FA Cup victory in 2001 when Liverpool defeated Arsenal.

A new, original Dr. Seuss book titled "What Pet Should I Get?" is set to be released on July 28, featuring the spirited siblings from "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish." The first printing of the book has been increased from 500,000 to 1 million copies due to high demand, and it marks the first new, original Dr. Seuss book since "Oh, the Places You'll Go!" in 1990. The manuscript for the new book was found in the authors' home after his death in 1991 and is believed to have been written between 1958 and 1962.

Jessica Carey surprised her grandmother, Patty Lawing, by getting a tattoo of a childhood portrait of her on her forearm. The tattoo was uncannily accurate, showing Patty as a young woman with long red hair, wearing a smart blouse and jacket. The surprise was captured on film, with Patty reacting emotionally, overwhelmed by the gesture. The video emerged online in February 2023, after Jessica shared it, stating that Patty is one of her favorite people in the world and the reaction is priceless.

Annegret Raunigk, a 65-year-old mother of 13 from Berlin, is due to break the record as the oldest woman to give birth to quadruplets. She is currently 21 weeks pregnant following 18 months of fertility treatment and is expecting the babies in the coming weeks. Despite the high risks associated with quadruplet pregnancies, particularly in women of her age, she expressed confidence in her ability to handle the delivery and has decided not to terminate the pregnancy. Raunigk made headlines previously in Germany for giving birth to her youngest daughter Leila at the age of 55.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, plans to deploy an unmanned rover, the SLIM probe, on the moon by 2018, aiming to perfect soft-landing technologies for potential future manned expeditions to the moon or even Mars. Estimated to cost around $83.4 million to $125 million, the mission, if approved, will utilize face recognition software to help the rover identify craters on the lunar surface. This move is seen as Japan's attempt to compete with its Asian counterparts China and India, who have achieved significant space milestones in recent years. If successful, Japan joins the United States, the former Soviet Union, and China as the only countries to have landed craft on the moon.

Dengue fever, a mosquito-borne disease, has affected several Brazilian football players, including Corinthians striker Paolo Guerrero, Palmeiras reserve goalkeeper Aranha, and Santos striker Leo Cittadini. The players have been advised to use insect repellent and avoid mosquito-prone areas during practice sessions. Over 460,000 cases of dengue fever have been reported in Brazil in 2015, with numerous deaths. Brazilian clubs are taking precautions to prevent further outbreaks among their players.

James Wilson, a Manchester United striker, expressed admiration for his teammates' skills, particularly Wayne Rooney's free-kick ability, Robin van Persie's movement, and Radamel Falcao's instincts. He believes Rooney's constant practice and accuracy in free kicks, Van Persie's ability to create space, and Falcao's knack for being in the right place in the 18-yard box are qualities he'd like to emulate. Wilson has 16 appearances for United this season, scoring one Premier League goal.

In Milwaukee, Wisconsin, a tragic incident occurred on Sunday evening. Archie Brown Jr, a father of four, was struck and killed after hitting a 2-year-old who ran into the street. Shortly after, an unidentified gunman opened fire at the scene, fatally shooting Brown Jr and a 15-year-old boy, whose connection to the incident is unclear. Police believe the shooting may have been in retaliation for the child's death, but they are still investigating and have yet to identify any suspects. The victim, Archie Brown Jr, was a real estate entrepreneur and landlord, leaving behind four daughters, the youngest only six months old.

A minor boy from Memphis, Tennessee has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers by posting pictures and videos that depict alleged gang life, including posing with guns, smoking suspicious substances, and using explicit language. This has prompted backlash from the community, with critics expressing concern for the boy's well-being and urging him to seek help and education. The boy's posts have been defended by some as a reflection of a difficult year, but others view them as perpetuating gang culture and potentially a threat to society. Authorities are becoming increasingly aware of social media as a tool for promoting gang culture, with around 50% of U.S. organized gangs maintaining a social media presence.

John Schumann, the former Redgum frontman, has criticized anti-Islam protesters for using his song, I Was Only 19, at their Reclaim Australia rallies. Schumann regards his music as promoting compassion, tolerance, and inclusiveness. The song, originally written to honor Vietnam veterans, was played at one of the rallies aiming to oppose sharia law, halal tax, and Islamization. The rallies resulted in violence between the protesters and anti-racism groups, with arrests occurring in Melbourne and Brisbane. Federal Opposition Leader Bill Shorten has condemned the violence, stating there is no place for it in any protests or expressions of free speech, and that any claims of Muslims planning to bring sharia law to Australia are exaggerated.

Emmanuel Adebayor, a striker for Tottenham Hotspur, has declared his intention to stay at the club and compete for a place, despite recent reports suggesting a move away. He labels the Premier League as the best in the world and voices thanks for the opportunity to play there. However, his performance this season has been underwhelming, with only two goals in 16 appearances, and with the emergence of Harry Kane, his future role with the team is uncertain. His last Premier League goal for Tottenham was against Newcastle in October 2015.

1. Stuart Pearce argues that Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini should be given more time to improve Manchester City's faltering performance, as the team faces a tough battle to secure a top-four finish and has been reduced to a dejected look in recent weeks.

2. Pearce, a former player and manager at City, cites the inconsistency of Yaya Toure as the primary reason for the team's poor performance, claiming that the Ivorian's declining form and scheduling conflicts during African Nations tours have contributed to the club's struggles.

3. Despite the club's underperforming squad this season, Sergio Aguero has emerged as a bright spot for Manchester City, delivering promising performances on the field.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce is optimistic about keeping the team in the Premier League despite a 2-0 defeat by Southampton, as they now face tough upcoming fixtures. Hull played better for the first half but ultimately lost due to a penalty and late goal. Bruce attributes their struggles to several long-term injuries to key players, and is confident they will survive the relegation battle. Southampton's James Ward-Prowse scored a penalty, with Sadio Mane trying to take it initially, causing issues in the team. Manager Ronald Koeman addressed this incident with the squad, reminding them of team rules.

A terror alert was triggered in Reading, England after a dummy wearing a balaclava and a fake missile launcher was spotted on a boat sailing down the Thames; police and an Army bomb disposal team were dispatched to the scene, but found the missile to be an ornament, not a live device. A local resident condemned the prank, expressing concerns about the potential panic it could cause, particularly given the proximity of the incident to a children's play area and recent events involving terrorism. The incident occurred just a few miles from Windsor Castle, where the Queen was in residence that week.

Tiger Woods endured a bizarre setback during the Masters tournament on Sunday, when he inadvertently struck a tree root with his club on the ninth hole, causing a ligament injury in his right wrist. Despite the pain, Woods managed to pop the ligament back into place and complete the competition at 5-under-par. Although he finished 13 strokes behind the eventual winner Jordan Spieth, Woods marked his best finish in over a year.

Iker Casillas, currently at Real Madrid, has stated he will remain at the club despite speculation linking David de Gea with a move to displace him as the first-choice keeper. Casillas, who began his career at Real Madrid as a teenager, is determined to fight for the Number 1 jersey he has made his own. He is focused on helping the team defend their Champions League title, with the semifinals promising to be exciting with the inclusion of fellow giants like Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and Juventus.

In Russia, a S300 missile launch failed spectacularly, with the rocket barely taking off before plummeting back to Earth. The incident resulted in a small explosion followed by a large plume of smoke, potentially causing embarrassment for President Vladimir Putin given the recent increase in the Russian defense budget. Remarkably, a second OTR-21 Tochka missile was launched from the wreckage soon after. This incident occurred in a region near Donetsk, Ukraine, where the missile was believed to be aimed at government forces.

Australian World Cup winner James Faulkner has been signed by Lancashire as their overseas player for most of the summer. Faulkner, who was named man of the match in the World Cup final against New Zealand, will replace compatriot Peter Siddle after his Indian Premier League stint. Lancashire head coach Ashley Giles is excited about the addition of Faulkner, who boasts impressive first-class cricket records, as he believes the all-rounder's white-ball skills at Emirates Old Trafford this season will be a significant boost to the team.

Jamie Carragher, a former Liverpool player and current Sky Sports pundit, traveled to Spain during the international break to watch his son James play for Liverpool's Under 12 team in the Mediterranean International Cup, a prestigious youth soccer tournament featuring over 200 clubs from 36 countries in Girona, Spain.
