The Liverpool squad, which includes Carragher's son, drew 1-1 with CE Mercantil and will face CE Cristinenc and FE ATL Bisbalenc in upcoming group stage matches. Notable alumni of the tournament include the likes of Philippe Coutinho, Lionel Messi, and Neymar.

Seattle-based filmmaker Gabriel Ng, during a three-month visit to Thailand, used a drone to film a six-minute love letter video showcasing the country's stunning beauty spots, including the picturesque coastline, religious sites, everyday life scenes, and islands like Ko Samui and Ko Phan. Notable attractions captured in the video are Wat Phra Yai (Big Buddha Temple), fishing boats on calm sea, waterfalls, mountains, and scenes from a street party. The high-definition video has received praise on YouTube for its professional quality, resembling footage from channels like the Discovery Channel.

Peter Moores, currently England's coach, expressed a willingness to work with Michael Vaughan, a potential new director of cricket for England, despite a past disagreement. Moores did not express the need for another voice in the team and was sad about the departure of Paul Downton, a key figure who brought Moores back to coaching. Vaughan is a leading candidate to replace Downton as managing director. Moores plans to stay focused on the upcoming Test series and remains committed to developing promising young players.

Nottingham Forest are planning to reinforce their attack by making a renewed offer for Blackburn Rovers' Jordan Rhodes this summer, priced at £10 million. Previously, Forest manager Dougie Freedman attempted to sign Rhodes on loan with a view to a permanent deal, an offer that was rejected by Blackburn in March. With 70 goals in the last three seasons, Rhodes is a coveted forward. Additionally, Blackburn's strike partner, Rudy Gestede with 19 goals this season, is attracting interest from Hull, Crystal Palace, West Brom, and Southampton.

In a unique musical performance, three domestic dogs - a Husky named Sky, and two Springer Spaniels, Sadie and Marshall - vocalized in harmony in their owner's house in Bahama, North Carolina. The video starts with Sadie barking, followed by Sky producing a melodious howl, which prompts Sadie to join in. The other Springer Spaniel, Marshall, moves excitedly around the room. The dogs harmonize further, pointing their noses towards the sky. The performance ends when the owner calls for quiet, surprising the dogs.

The 'French Spiderman', Alain Robert, climbed Dubai's 1,007ft twisted skyscraper, the Cayan Tower, without a safety harness, using only sticky tape and chalk for assistance. Hundreds of spectators watched as Robert completed the 75-storey climb in approximately an hour and a half. The French climber, who has a history of falls during previous climbs, is known for illegally ascending buildings worldwide. This climb was captured on video and showed Robert struggling to find footholds on the narrow ledges, at one point waving a flag in homage to the tower's developers. Interestingly, in 2011, Robert also climbed the world's tallest tower, the Burj Khalifa, but used a rope and harness to comply with regulations.

1. An experimental cancer drug discontinued due to poor cancer treatment results, AZDO5030, has shown promise in reversing the effects of Alzheimer's, as revealed in a study conducted at Yale University.

2. The treatment achieved this by blocking a process that breaks nerve connections in the brain used for memory storage, and consequently, restored memory in mice affected by Alzheimer's.

3. Human trials for the drug have been initiated to test its efficacy in Alzheimer's patients, led by researchers Stephen Strittmatter and Christopher van Dyck, as efforts continue to combat the growing issue of Alzheimer's in the UK, with an estimated one million people expected to have the disease by 2025 and an annual cost of £26 billion.

1. Paul Bettany will play the Vision, a longtime member of the Avengers in the comics, in the upcoming "Avengers: Age of Ultron" movie. Marvel Studios released a poster confirming his character.
2. In yesterday's announcements, Marvel revealed the real Daredevil suit for Netflix's new series, unveiled the character of Angel for the upcoming "X-Men: Apocalypse" film, and shared the first look of Jamie Bell as The Thing in the rebooted "Fantastic Four" movie.
3. The article concludes that with multiple new superhero announcements within a day, the superhero trend in films remains strong, with notable new releases this year including "Avengers: Age of Ultron", "Fantastic Four", and the Netflix series "Daredevil".

Veteran referee Kenny Bayless, who has worked several of Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao's fights, has been appointed as the third man in the ring for their highly anticipated match. However, some, including Oscar De La Hoya, a past opponent of Mayweather, believe Bayless' appointment could potentially give Mayweather an advantage due to his refereeing style, which favors Mayweather in clinches. De La Hoya lost the WBC light middleweight title to Mayweather in a split decision in 2007.

1. Harry Kane's participation in England's Under-21 European Championship is uncertain due to his commitment to a friendly match with Tottenham in Malaysia, scheduled for May 27.
2. Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino has expressed concerns about burnout for Kane, with discussions ongoing about his availability for the tournament.
3. Kane, who captained his team against Burnley, has been excluded from England's senior friendly against the Republic of Ireland and the Euro 2016 qualifier against Slovenia, to ensure he gets adequate rest before next season.

The California measles outbreak that started in December 2021, primarily affecting over 130 individuals, has been declared over by the California Department of Public Health. This is because there has been no new case of the B3 strain for 42 days, a period equivalent to two successive incubation periods. The health department attributed the containment of the outbreak to swift investigation and subsequent vaccination of at-risk individuals, as well as increased awareness among healthcare providers about measles. The outbreak first started among visitors to two Disney theme parks in California, with 42 of the cases occurring from December 17-20. Despite identifying two patients with rashes in April, they had a different measles genotype, indicating a separate occurrence.

A family-of-six was sighted in San Miguel de Tucuman, Argentina, riding on a single motorbike without helmets. The arrangement included a man holding the handlebars, three young children on the petrol tank, a girl and a woman on the seat behind, and another child in front. Witnesses have described the scene as shocking and dangerous, prompting widespread condemnation on social media. Similar instances involving families riding on a single motorbike have occurred recently in other Argentine cities. Police are currently seeking the parents involved in these incidents, stating the behavior as irresponsible and dangerous.

Andrea McVeigh, a 44-year-old social media manager, was severely injured after being knocked down by a cyclist on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London. The cyclist fled the scene, but CCTV footage has been released by the Met Police in an attempt to identify the cyclist. McVeigh sustained significant facial injuries, including two three-inch gashes to her forehead, and is currently off work sick due to her injuries and fear of being on the street. The police are appealing for help in identifying the cyclist and have launched a hunt for the individual responsible for the incident.

The headstone of Hillary Clinton's father, Hugh Rodham, was found tipped over in Scranton, Pennsylvania, two days after Clinton announced her run for the White House. The gravestone is located at the Washburn Street Cemetery, and local resident Paul McGloin, who tends to the site, found it tipped over. Police are investigating the incident, suspecting vandalism as the most likely cause, although they continue to consider the possibility of weather involvement. Some, like McGloin, have speculated about a connection between the vandalism and Clinton's presidential bid.

A California woman, Beatriz Paez, was terrified when a Deputy U.S. Marshal took her cell phone during a recording of police activity, smashing it with his foot. The incident occurred in South Gate, California. Paez has since filed a complaint and is considering a lawsuit. The U.S. Marshals Service is reviewing the incident, and U.S. Representative Janice Hahn has written a letter to outgoing U.S. Attorney General Eric Holder requesting a federal investigation into the actions of the officer involved, as Paez was not hindering an investigation or arrest.

Max, a husky-corgi mix, is currently residing at the Dogs Trust in Basildon, Essex, having been abandoned. Despite his small stature (18.5in), Max is a fully grown adult dog and has captivated the staff with his gentleness, intelligence, and heartiness. The popularity of huskies in part stems from shows like Game of Thrones, leading to a trend where many new owners struggle to meet their unique exercise and socialization needs, often resulting in abandonment.

Chilean pickpockets have surpassed other groups to become the most effective thieves in central London, targeting wealthy shoppers in the West End. They are known for operating in groups of three to six, often blending in as families or businesspeople. The Metropolitan Police have arrested Chilean women carrying large amounts of cash and valuable jewelry, while many other international gangs such as Romanians, Algerians, and Bulgarians also target London's busy shopping areas. According to Detective Constable Darren Bond, these organized international gangs often move between cities to avoid detection, but his team has seen a 50% reduction in thefts over the last year.

A 20-year-old man survived a severe car accident where his vehicle flipped over and landed on him, trapping him. Firefighters used 25 minutes to free him from the car. The man suffered head, chest, and possibly leg fractures but miraculously remained conscious. Emergency services, including multiple ambulances, fire engines, police, and the Warwickshire and Northamptonshire air ambulance responded to the accident scene in Southam, Warwickshire. The man was airlifted to the University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire with multiple injuries including head, chest, pelvic, and leg fractures. The ambulance service praised the quick response and early treatment efforts by their community paramedic who was first on scene. Firefighters used specialized cutting equipment and glass stabilization pack to rescue the trapped man before he was transported to the hospital.

A gang of fly-tippers dumped an estimated 40 tonnes of industrial waste in a Suffolk village, leaving a pile described as the worst in almost 30 years by a rural crime officer. This illegal act, believed to involve three tractors and trailers, includes materials from the carpet and veterinary industries. Efforts to prevent fly-tipping include a campaign by police, the National Farmers' Union, and the Country Land and Business Association. Local authorities are now working to remove the waste from the roadside.

A man was Tasered at Pearson International Airport in Toronto after refusing to comply with security protocol, attempting to enter a restricted area, and aggressively resisting attempts to communicate with him. The incident was captured on video by a bystander, showing the man being Tasered, standing for a few seconds before being brought to the ground by police, and being handcuffed. The man was later taken to a nearby hospital under Canada's Mental Health Act, and it is not clear whether authorities will be seeking criminal charges against him.

An incident forced a government jet carrying Serbia's president to turn back during a flight to Italy last week. The cause was traced to a co-pilot spilling coffee on the instrument board, which activated the emergency slat button, causing the plane to lose altitude. The pilot took immediate control, landed the plane safely in Belgrade, and the president had to cancel his official visit to the Vatican. The pilot's license was temporarily suspended due to the incident involving the aged, problematic aircraft.

In South Africa, over 300 suspects have been arrested for deadly attacks on foreigners in Durban, forcing thousands to flee. The government has condemned these attacks, praising law enforcement for preventing further bloodshed. Notable acts of support have come from South Africans and the Gift of the Givers charity, which is assisting displaced individuals. The history of South Africa, including the support received from African neighbors during the Apartheid, is being invoked to encourage understanding and unity amidst this xenophobic sentiment.

A skier, Zach Birnie, was caught in an avalanche while skiing off-piste in Revelstoke, Canada. The incident was recorded on a helmet camera. The skier initially seemed to ski cautiously but suddenly fell as thick snow buried his skis. Panicked, he struggled to find the surface of the snow. Fortunately, he emerged later, reporting minor injuries such as a pulled shoulder and lost pole. Cornelia Accola from the WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF speculated that the avalanche was triggered by the amount of fresh snow and steep terrain. She also advised to escape an avalanche area, let go of ski poles, try to open bindings, pull knees towards chest, and hold arms in front of the face if caught in a similar situation.

On the hottest day of the year, two men robbed an Esso petrol station in Surrey, stripping off their shirts before the robbery. The men entered the manager's office of the filling station in Caterham, looking for cash. Surrey Police have released CCTV images of the men in hopes of identifying them, announcing that a third man has been arrested and released on police bail while the investigation continues.

The article discusses the Lada Niva 4x4, a rugged and affordable SUV from Russia that might see increased sales due to the Land Rover Defender's discontinuation. Priced at £13,395 on the road, the Niva has gained a cult following for its robust nature and chunky looks, despite its Soviet era origins. The interior is minimalistic and easy to clean, but a previous Russian President, Vladimir Putin, upgraded his Niva with a German engine in 2009.

The AIDS Healthcare Foundation, the nation's largest HIV and AIDS medical care provider, is being accused of a $20 million dollar scam involving kickbacks for patient referrals in a lawsuit filed by three former managers in South Florida federal court. The lawsuit claims that employees were offered $100 bonuses for referring patients with positive test results to the company's clinics and pharmacies, with the alleged practice starting in 2010 at the company's California headquarters and expanding to multiple locations. The company, which cares for over 400,000 patients in 36 countries, denies the allegations and asserts its actions are crucial for HIV detection and treatment.

The bearded dragon named Liz appears to understand English as she nods when her owner asks if she's hungry. Liz at mealtime with owner Shannen Hussein is the subject of a recent video. Liz, who is kept at Shannen's hobby farm and is a popular social media pet, loves superworm treats and responds affirmatively to the question "Are you hungry?" Other pets on the farm, including a pet lamb named Winter, are also social media sensations.

A West Virginia resident, Travis Hatfield, has gained viral fame for his heartfelt rendition of a George Jones hit to his uncle, Jamie Joe Cline, who has Down syndrome. The video, which has garnered over 410,00 views, showcases the two musical companions belting out the song He Stopped Loving Her Today. Travis, an aspiring country singer, shares that his uncle's love for music is stronger than his own and that the pair enjoy weekly music sessions, spanning various country artists from George Jones to Jason Aldean. With newfound popularity and offers from Nashville record labels, Travis plans to audition for The Voice 2016 and release a CD of original songs, hoping to secure a record deal that his family can be proud of.

Nik Wallenda, a seventh-generation high-wire performer, has announced his upcoming stunt to walk untethered atop the 400-foot Orlando Eye observation wheel in Florida on April 29. Notable for its size and absence of a pole, this feat will take place as the wheel is in motion.best known for previous walks across the Grand Canyon, Niagara Falls, and Chicago skyscrapers, Wallenda has cited this latest challenge as unique in his career.

Bayern Munich central defender Medhi Benatia, 27, sustained a muscle injury and is expected to be out for between two and four weeks, which could cause him to miss both legs of their Champions League quarter-final against Porto. This adds to Bayern's already extensive injury list that includes several key players. Despite these setbacks, Bayern, who are 10 points clear at the top of the Bundesliga, continue to aim for domestic and European titles, with players like Franck Ribery and Thiago Alcantara returning to training.

Bayern Munich, managed by Pep Guardiola, clinched a berth in the Champions League semifinals after a 6-1 victory over Porto, bringing their season goal tally to an astonishing 115 goals. With five Bundesliga matches, the German Cup semifinals, and potentially more Champions League games remaining, the team seems unstoppable and is on track for a third consecutive title. Notable goal scorers this season include Robert Lewandowski, Thiago Alcantara, Sebastian Rode, Arjen Robben, Mario Gotze, Jerome Boateng, and Holger Badstuber.

Former Atletico Madrid striker Fernando Torres credits manager Diego Simeone for the team's recent success, including their unbeaten run against Real Madrid in six matches. Simeone is known for his emphasis on team cohesion, understanding their strengths and weaknesses, and playing at their limit. Several key players are one yellow card away from suspension for the Champions League quarter-final match.

A small aircraft en route from central Scotland to Tiree, the most westerly island of the inner Hebrides, crashed near Loch Etive in western Scotland, resulting in the discovery of the bodies of two passengers. Search and rescue operations involving helicopters, lifeboats, and the police were launched after the plane lost radar contact near Beinn Nan Lus. Police are investigating the circumstances of the crash and urge anyone with information to contact them.

A bus crashed into a Boeing 777 jet, believed to be an Uzbekistan Airways plane, at Tashkent airport, Uzbekistan. The damage is substantial, but details about potential engine damage or injuries are unavailable. The busy airport is likely to have had delays as a result. Incidents like this are unfortunately becoming more frequent, with multiple instances of plane collisions occurring at various airports, including Dublin and Heathrow airports. The exact circumstances leading up to these crashes are often unclear, but fortunately, no significant injuries have been reported.

An off-duty Secret Service agent, Arthur Baldwin, was arrested in Washington D.C. early Friday morning on charges of attempted burglary and destruction of property. Baldwin was posted with the Foreign Missions Branch of the service, which works with the State Department on diplomatic activities. His arrest follows another high-ranking official being put on leave for misconduct allegations, both incidents are currently under investigation. These recent incidents have added to the agency's reputation issues, particularly regarding an incident in March involving two high-ranking officials driving into a secure area at the White House.

Israel is developing a cutting-edge tunnel detection system, jointly created by Elbit Systems and the Israeli Ministry of Defense, to prevent false alarms. The system, predicted to cost around £2.3 million ($3.5m) per mile, will primarily focus on the land border between Gaza and Israel and is aimed at providing additional security. The project, which follows years of conflict between Israel and Gaza, has reportedly been underway for a year and had successfully passed initial trials.

A primary school headteacher, Linda Shute, has implemented a policy banning all drinks except water at Rowdown Primary School in New Addington, south London, citing long-term health benefits. Some parents disagreed, arguing that their children dislike water and feel the rule is too restrictive. The opposition has launched a campaign to change the policy, claiming it infringes on parental rights to choose what their children drink. The school acknowledges the concerns but stands by the decision to enforce the water-only rule for the children's long-term health. The controversy follows similar incidents at other schools. Some expertsback the policy, noting that sugar-filled juices should be limited due to high sugar content.

Boxer Paul Smith has secured a highly challenging fight against Andre Ward in Oakland, California on June 20th. This fight is not for Ward's WBA super-middleweight world title. Smith, a former title challenger who failed to clinch the WBO belt twice, will face a formidable opponent in Ward, who has been inactive since 2013. Smith, expressing excitement, views this encounter as an opportunity to test himself against a top-tier boxer and hopes to leverage his freshness and ring confidence to win. Ward, on the other hand, is excited to be fighting in his hometown, acknowledging the tough competition Smith presents but intends to defend his title with a strong performance.

Angela Merkel and her husband, Joachim Sauer, are spending their annual Easter holiday in Italy at the five-star Miramare Spa Hotel on Ischia. Due to the cooler weather, Merkel has reportedly been avoiding the pool and lounges and instead is taking Pilates classes and enjoying vegetarian meals. Her husband, a professor of theoretical chemistry, rarely appears in public and has steered clear of the media spotlight throughout their marriage.

Ander Herrera, a midfielder for Manchester United, scored a brace against Aston Villa with his eyes closed, adding to his history of scoring without looking at the ball or the goal. This unusual technique has caught the attention of manager Louis van Gaal, who praised Herrera's shooting ability but encouraged him to control the ball before shooting. Despite this unconventional method, Herrera has been instrumental in several key Manchester United wins.

A 23-month-old girl was tragically killed when her father accidentally struck her with a pickup truck in Nevada, not aware she was in the driveway. The incident took place on Thursday in a North Las Vegas neighborhood and the girl later succumbed to her injuries at University Medical Hospital. The police declared the incident an accident, and no charges will be filed, according to the Las Vegas Review-Journal. The girl was days away from her second birthday. The identities of the father, toddler, and other family members involved in the incident have not been disclosed.

The University of Connecticut's baseball team has welcomed a new member, 5-year-old Grayson Hand who is battling leukemia, through the help of Team IMPACT. Grayson, who now has his own locker with the team, will be able to attend games and practices. His 7-year-old sister, Sophie, was named an honorary cheerleader. Father Nate Hand described the partnership as a physical representation of the outpouring of emotional support they've received.

A passenger on a London Midland train from Lichfield Trent Valley to Longbridge discovered excrement in a newspaper on the floor, causing a severe delay due to the cleaning of the carriage. The incident was described as "disgusting" by London Midland, who promised to provide CCTV images of the suspect to the police. This act of vandalism caused significant disruption to commuters on the Cross City line, with normal service resuming around 9:30am. A similar incident occurred last month on a British Airways flight to Dubai, where a flight was aborted due to a smelly bathroom.

James Rodriguez, the Real Madrid midfielder, has been praised for seamlessly settling into his new team, with Marca claiming he is worth his weight in gold. The Colombian star has scored 13 goals and provided 12 assists since his £60million move from Monaco, and his presence in the side has significantly improved Real Madrid's win rate. In contrast, Cristiano Ronaldo's appeal against a yellow card for diving is the focus of another Spanish newspaper, AS. Meanwhile, Italian paper La Gazzetta dello Sport reports on Roberto Mancini's plans for a summer revamp at Inter Milan, with a list of 21 potential signings including Premier League players Yaya Toure, Filipe Luis, and Lucas Leiva, as well as Barcelona's Pedro and Palermo forward Paulo Dybala. Tuttosport also features an interview with Juventus striker Alvaro Morata, who expresses no interest in rejoining Real Madrid and compares Juve to Atletico Madrid's unexpected run in the Champions League.

A Florida man, Kenneth Crowder, was arrested in Melbourne after running naked through a neighborhood, claiming to be God, and engaging in unspecified lewd behavior on a tree. He was later identified as being under the influence of Flakka, a designer drug said to be stronger than crystal meth. Flakka, which usually contains the chemical alpha-PVP, is known for inducing feelings of euphoria, hallucinations, and sometimes psychosis or superhuman strength. In 2014, there were over 670 reported Flakka occurrences in Florida, indicating a growing problem with the drug.

A Russian Premier League match between Arsenal Tula and Torpedo Moscow was suspended for seven minutes due to fighting caused by Torpedo fans breaking down barriers, attempting to enter the East Stand where women and children were sitting, and throwing chairs at law enforcement officers and stewards. The incident led to an on-field brawl and fights on the running track. Referees temporarily halted the match, and after order was restored, Torpedo won 3-1. Due to the fans' repeated violent behavior, the team is expected to receive a severe punishment. Torpedo has previously been punished for racist behavior of their supporters, and this is not their first disruption of a match this season.

High school girls in Huizhou, China are undergoing intense military-style knife fighting training under the instruction of ex-special forces soldier Inspector Tan. The training, which includes eight moves to defend against attackers, uses fake knives with plastic retractable blades to ensure safety. This self-defense training is part of a broader program for all female students at the school to help them recognize dangerous situations. The training, which takes five days, is popular among the students due to its effectiveness and practical application in everyday life, including the use of everyday objects like chopsticks for self-defense.

AP McCoy, champion jockey since 1997, will retire if his mount, Shutthefrontdoor, wins the Grand National on Saturday. Shutthefrontdoor is garnering emotional support as the horse to deliver a second Grand National victory for McCoy. McCoy acknowledges the unpredictable nature of jump racing and remains hopeful for a fairytale ending to his career.

Tennis player John Isner, a 6-foot-10 American, advanced to the Miami Open semifinals by defeating Kei Nishikori 6-4, 6-3. Isner, known for his powerful serve, had not faced break points in the tournament and won the last eight points of the first set to clinch it. Meanwhile, Andy Murray, the former number one, will face Tomas Berdych in the other semi-final, marking a reunion of sorts, as Berdych's coach, Jez Green, was formerly Murray's fitness coach. This match carries a potential for tension, as Murray previously defeated Berdych in this year's Australian Open semi-final. Previous heated encounters between the two prompted frustration from Murray's wife, Kim Sears, who was witnessed uttering expletives during their Australian Open match.

German football legend Franz Beckenbauer criticized Bayern Munich's performance in their Champions League quarter-final defeat against Porto, labeling it as if the players had taken "sleeping pills." He specifically accused defender Dante of playing poorly, likening his performance to wearing "ski boots." The former Bayern Munich coach also commented on the difference between the team's domestic and international performance.

A 21-year-old man, Arnold Quintero from San Antonio, Texas, has been arrested on multiple charges including aggravated sexual assault of a child, following allegations of imprisonment, beating, sexual assault, and burning a 13-year-old girl with a lighter. The girl was held captive in a 'trap house' between January 21 and February 8, during which she was punched, photographed, and sexually assaulted. The Bexar County Sheriff’s Office is currently investigating the case, and as of Friday night, Quintero remains in jail facing three outstanding charges.

World No 1 Michael van Gerwen had a mixed night in Week 12 of the Betway Premier League in Cardiff, winning impressively against James Wade (7-0) but losing to Gary Anderson (5-7) in the final match. Van Gerwen maintained his spot in the play-offs, while Anderson's night included a loss to Stephen Bunting (1-7) but a win over Van Gerwen. Additional matches saw Raymond van Barneveld defeating Dave Chisnall (7-5), Phil Taylor drawing with Adrian Lewis (6-6), and Stephen Bunting beating Gary Anderson (7-1).

In summary, British training consultant Jay Rutland, 34, married to billionaire heiress Tamara Ecclestone, saw his firm Brigante Business Developments bring in just £3,378 in the year up to July 2014, despite being valued at £18,131 the year prior. The firm offers management consultancy but was not actively trading during the reported period. Rutland previously worked as a stockbroker in the City of London but was banned from trading in 2012 for market abuse. He has a net worth significantly lower than his wife's family, which is estimated to be worth £3 billion. Despite their wealth, the couple recently celebrated their daughter Sophia's first birthday with a farmyard-themed party estimated to cost £70,000, including luxury gifts like ponies, a zebra, a balloon house, a magical princess, and a replica electric Bentley car toy.

A leukaemia patient, Jia Binhui, 25, unable to afford further hospital treatment, resorted to an unconventional treatment by lying on a barbecue-like structure in his garden, claiming it could kill the cancerous cells in his body at temperatures over 42 degrees Celsius. Jia, a resident of Yunlong County, Yunnan Province, China, had previously undergone a £55,000 bone marrow transplant funded by well-wishers. Married last month to Liu Yuan, Jia continues his homemade treatment while hoping for improvement in his condition before returning to the hospital.

Queens Park Rangers midfielder Leroy Fer, who has been sidelined with a knee injury since February, could return to the squad for the London derby against West Ham, according to manager Chris Ramsey. Despite struggles for form and fitness, Fer is "in contention" for the game, with Ramsey acknowledging the club is taking a risk to try and bolster their efforts against relegation. Other players also returning to fitness for QPR include defender Richard Dunne and Korean left-back Yun Suk-Young, but Rio Ferdinand remains unavailable.

1. In the Scheldeprijs race on Wednesday, Team Sky riders Sir Bradley Wiggins and Geraint Thomas managed to avoid a major crash, but their teammate Elia Viviani wasn't so fortunate.
2. Viviani was involved in a crash that sent around 50 riders to the ground and caused him to go to the hospital for x-rays, with injuries reported in his arm and ribs.
3. Wiggins and Thomas were part of a strong Team Sky line-up in the race, with the incident happening at the end of the race just before the expected sprint finish for Viviani. This was Viviani's penultimate race for Team Sky before the Paris-Roubaix, while the team's sports director, Servais Knaven, noted that the rest of the team members were in good shape for the upcoming Paris-Roubaix. The eventual winner was Katusha's Alexander Kristoff with only 14 riders contesting the sprint following the crash.

Aston Villa players received messages of encouragement from fans in their dressing room before the FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool. Jack Grealish thanked fans on Twitter, sharing a personal message from supporter Mike Shenaniganz Cope. Coach Tim Sherwood included Grealish in the starting line-up due to his recent impressive performances, and goalkeeper Brad Guzan also revealed a message from a fan telling the team to "fight like Lions."

A 12-year-old named Hanghang in central China was seriously injured when his old phone exploded while charging, exposing part of his jawbone and embedding fragments in his arms and legs. Doctors believe the most common cause of the explosion was improper charging, resulting from overheating and poor contact. Hanghang, now being treated in a hospital, is expected to need several operations to repair the damage. He stated that the battery likely exploded, and he had heard of similar incidences but never thought it would happen to him.

Mike Rowe, host of "Somebody's Gotta Do It," met with Chad Pregracke, founder of Living Lands & Waters, a non-profit organization dedicated to cleaning up U.S. waterways. Pregracke, who was awarded CNN Hero of the Year in 2013, aims to remove 500,000 more pounds of trash in 2015 with the help of volunteers. His unique 150-foot solar-powered barge, previously a recycled strip club, serves as part home, part office, and part dumpster for his team during cleanups. To get involved, visit LivingLandsAndWaters.org/Get-Involved/.

The abandoned ghost town of Balestrino, dating back to the 11th century, was once home to 800 inhabitants but was left uninhabited due to seismic instability, with significant damage caused by an earthquake in 1887. Today, the crumbling structures and castle on the hill give a haunting eeriness to the town, earning it the reputation as Italy's most famous abandoned location, often rumored to be haunted. A recently shot drone footage highlights the town's decay, showcasing the grandeur of the castle contrasted with the other dilapidated buildings.

The article describes a Star Wars event where director J.J. Abrams and the cast of Episode VII - The Force Awakens showed a trailer and discussed aspects of the upcoming film. Highlights include Han Solo and Chewbacca's return, a new planet setting called Jakku, hints about Luke and Leia's involvement, less CGI than in the prequels, and the presence of a crashed Star Destroyer. The event was met with enthusiasm by the audience, prompting excited reactions on social media.

Rob Ford, the former Toronto Mayor, has announced that he will undergo surgery to remove a cancerous tumor in his abdomen on May 11. He has shared that the tumor, initially diagnosed as malignant liposarcoma, has been significantly shrunk through chemotherapy and radiation. Ford hopes for a recovery by September and a return to work as a councilor. The surgery is expected to last eight to ten hours and will be carried out by four surgeons.

A South African university has removed the statue of British colonialist Cecil Rhodes following weeks of protests by students who consider his legacy symbols of racism and supremacy. The decision follows a campaign led by the university's Students' Representative Council, which demanded the statue's removal. However, the act has sparked a controversy, with some arguing that removing the statue is an attempt to erase history rather than engaging with it. In a contrasting move, protesters in Pretoria chained themselves to a statue of another historical figure, Paul Kruger, in response to the removal of Rhodes' statue. The debate raises questions about how history should be approached and commemorated.

Michael Phelps returned to competitive racing after a six-month suspension, marking his comeback with a 100 meters butterfly victory at the Arena Pro Swim Series in Arizona. Despite the setback, he revealed his intention to compete at the 2016 Olympics in Rio de Janeiro, making him aim for a fifth Olympic Games. The most decorated Olympian in history, Phelps missed this summer's World Championships in Kazan, Russia, following discussions with USA Swimming.

A New York woman was found hanging from a third-floor fire escape of her apartment building in Crown Heights on Sunday morning. The incident left witnesses traumatized, with one individual initially suspecting it was a Halloween prank. The woman's identity has not been release pending notifying her family, and neighbors described her as a friendly and social individual who struggled with mental health issues. The National Suicide Prevention Lifeline number (1-800-273-8255) is provided for confidential help.

1. Lyon and Saint-Etienne played a 2-2 draw in the Rhone Valley derby, with Lyon moving back to the top of Ligue 1 due to Paris St Germain having a game in hand. Clinton N'Jie, Romain Hamouma, and Christophe Jallet scored the goals.

2. Lille won 2-0 against Bordeaux, with Nolan Roux and Adama Traore finding the back of the net. This was their sixth win in seven games, moving them four points behind Bordeaux and keeping them in contention for fourth place.

3. Montpellier beat Caen 1-0, with Brazilian defender Hilton scoring the only goal early in the game. The win moved Montpellier up to seventh in the standings, while Caen dropped to 13th with four points from their last six matches.

1. Arsene Wenger admits he did not anticipate Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin's significant contributions to Arsenal's late push for the Premier League title.
2. Bellerin, who was previously on loan at Watford, scored a vital goal against Liverpool, demonstrating his impressive progress at only 20 years old.
3. Despite a close call with a possible red card, Wenger praised Bellerin's defense and mental quality, indicating there is still room for the young player to grow and gain more experience.

Fox is developing a two-hour remake of "The Rocky Horror Picture Show," originally released in 1975, directed by Kenneth Ortega (High School Musical). The project, titled "The Rocky Horror Picture Show Event," is under production by Fox 21 Television Studios and The Jackal Group, with Gail Berman and Lou Adler involved as executive producers. The special, scheduled to celebrate the film's 40th anniversary, will not air live but features no further confirmed details yet.

Roman football club AS Roma has been ordered to partially close their stadium for an upcoming game after offensive banners were displayed during their match against Napoli, mocking the mother of a Napoli supporter who was killed in violent clashes last year. The banners caused outrage, and the Serie A disciplinary tribunal described them as "provocatively insulting." AS Roma's stadium will be part-closed for the league match with Atalanta on April 19 due to the sanction. The deceased Napoli fan's mother, Antonella Leardi, expressed disappointment and called for an end to football violence. AS Roma's club president, James Pallotta, condemned the fans responsible and expressed deep sympathy for the families affected by the tragedy.

Ellen White, the Notts County footballer, had a memorable night as she scored against her former club Arsenal in the Women's Super League. The goal came from a well-executed free kick in the 26th minute that caught Arsenal off guard due to confusion among defenders Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood. Additionally, White missed a penalty that could have given Notts County a 2-0 lead, and Arsenal later equalized with a late goal by Chioma Ubogagu.

Arsene Wenger acknowledges discussions about signing Eden Hazard from Lille in 2012, but could not afford him due to financial constraints, with Chelsea eventually securing him for £32million. Wenger admits that Hazard's performance this season suggests it might have been a missed opportunity, but feels the decision was unavoidable due to the financial climate at the time. Wenger also suggests that Alexis Sanchez will pose a strong challenge to Hazard for the Player of the Season award, admiring Hazard's maturity, improved final ball, and ability to turn games in tight situations.

Stephen Akers-Belcher, the former mayor of Hartlepool, was dismissed from his care manager role with Newcastle City Council for gross misconduct after he was pictured attending HMS Warrior during a paid leave supposedly taken for compassionate reasons. The photos revealed Akers-Belcher was 323 miles away from his jurisdiction. Akers-Belcher had initially claimed he was attending a funeral during the leave period but failed to provide evidence supporting this claim. Newcastle City Council denied that the dismissal was a result of whistle-blowing and stated they treated his allegations with utmost seriousness, carrying out independent investigations that resulted in no further action. Akers-Belcher has since refused to comment on the incident.

A highly experienced general practitioner, Doctor John Parker, who had been working at an Australian-run Ebola treatment clinic in Sierra Leone since November 2014, tested negative for the Ebola virus after developing influenza-like symptoms and being treated at Westmead Hospital in Sydney. He had followed protocol and notified authorities upon his return to Australia as a precaution. The World Health Organization has reported over 10,000 deaths from the Ebola virus in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

A 9-year-old England-based football prodigy, Frankie Franz, mimicked Barcelona's Martin Montoya by scoring a basketball-style goal from 27 yards twice, into a basketball hoop placed in the garden. The youngster's accuracy astounded his mother and himself, much like the original clip of Montoya's trick shot at Barcelona's Ciutat Esportiva training ground. Frankie's football dream includes playing for Real Madrid or Barcelona.

The Wisden–MCC Cricket Photograph of the Year 2014 showcases a global range of cricket images, from professional matches to informal games. Matthew Lewis won the competition with his photo of Dwayne Bravo taking a breathtaking catch for the West Indies during the ICC World Twenty20 against Australia. The list also includes diverse scenes, such as children playing in a Bangladesh rubbish tip and club players in Kent.

A New Jersey judge has ruled in favor of a mother who took her 11-year-old daughter to a Pink concert, dismissing the father's claims of "abusing parental discretion." The judge found the mother did not exceed reasonable judgment in allowing the child to attend the show, as the girl was "dying to go" and the performance was deemed age-appropriate after the mother researched clips on YouTube. The judge also highlighted Pink's music as containing messages suitable for adolescents, despite some suggestive elements.

1. Salcombe, a coastal town in Devon, has become the most expensive place in the UK to buy property, with an average cost of £671,759, surpassing London's average of £638,217. This is due to a 10% increase in property prices over the past 12 months.

2. The average value of a waterfront property in Salcombe is a staggering £2 million, making it more expensive than several upscale London neighborhoods, including Notting Hill, Regent's Park, and Hampstead Heath.

For those who want to experience this millionaire lifestyle without breaking the bank, the Salcombe Harbour Hotel offers waterfront rooms starting from £425 during the summer season.

2. In response, the SFA has stated that all four participating clubs were consulted on ticket pricing, and the prices have remained unchanged for the past four years. They also noted that the gate, broadcast, and advertising revenues for both semi-finals are aggregated and distributed evenly among the teams.

A pupil, Rebecca Rice, brought her pet Labrador, Holly, into a GCSE exam to help her cope with severe nerves. This decision was made after consultation with teacher Lorette Esteve, who also assisted in reducing stress for other students at Bodmin College, Cornwall, by allowing items like drinks, lucky key rings, or a friend in the exam room. Rebecca found hosting Holly during her French oral test particularly helpful, confirming that it helped calm her nerves during the examination.

Anders Lindegaard, the third-choice goalkeeper at Manchester United, enjoys a happy life off the pitch with his wife Misse Beqiri, a Swedish model with Albanian roots. They married last year in a romantic beach wedding in Mauritius and have a son together. Despite limited playing time at Old Trafford, Lindegaard frequently posts about his family on Instagram, reminding fans of his marriage. Manchester United goalkeepers David de Gea and Victor Valdes took a break from their professional duties and visited a theme park on Tuesday, enjoying a relaxing day out amidst United's impressive winning streak in the Premier League. United have improved their position in the league, challenging Arsenal for second place after struggling earlier in the season. However, the future of both Valdes and De Gea at Old Trafford is uncertain, leaving a question mark over where they will be spending their summers.

John Goodwin, a 75-year-old piano teacher, shot himself outside the Rockingham County Superior Courthouse in New Hampshire on Friday morning during jury deliberations on charges of aggravated felonious sexual assault against an underage student. Prosecutors alleged Goodwin repeatedly assaulted the student, now 24, while his defense attorney stated his client was 'touchy-feely' but did not commit a crime. Goodwin's health status remains undisclosed, and the jury was still deliberating as of Friday afternoon. Further details are expected to be released by the New Hampshire Attorney General's Office later that evening.

Amazon has removed a computer game titled "Rescue the Anorexia Girl" from its platform due to backlash. The game, which was marketed by SmartTouch media and available on Amazon and Android, invited players to throw food at a cartoon girl character who is depicted as having anorexia. The game's instructions promoted the idea that players could save the character from her illness. Social media users have criticized the game for further stigmatizing people with eating disorders and for promoting harmful stereotypes. Brian Cuban, a blogger who has dealt with eating disorders, stated that such games do not address the biological and complex nature of eating disorders and may deter individuals from seeking help.

Researchers, notably the Green Brain Project team, aim to recreate the cognitive abilities of European Honeybees to power drones. The focus is on creating a robot that thinks, senses, and acts like the honeybee. Although they've achieved cloning the part of the bee's brain responsible for sight, they're currently developing more complex functions, conducting tests in a dedicated flying room at the University of Sheffield. The eventual goal is to have these robots assist with tasks like crop pollination or search and rescue missions.

A newly-wed couple, both employees of Air Malta, embarked on a romantic flight over the Mediterranean to celebrate their wedding. The Airbus A319 flight took an unusual heart-shaped route, with stops around Malta and skirting the Italian coast, at one point passing near Mount Etna. Some social media users speculated the flight was for training purposes or a publicity stunt, while Air Malta confirmed it was a special private flight for the newlyweds and their guests.

A giraffe named Melvin was gored to death by an eland antelope at Kristiansand Zoo in Norway, with around 30 people, including many children, witnessing the unprovoked attack. Melvin, who was born at the zoo in 2010 and was a favorite among young visitors, had gotten his head stuck in the enclosure's fence before the attack. Veterinary efforts to save Melvin were unsuccessful, and the cause of the antelope's aggressive behavior remains unknown.

The restaurant manager at Rubens eatery in Leuven, Belgium, has been labeled the 'stingiest boss in Europe' for charging a mother 36p to heat up her baby's feeding bottle. The mother, Gitte Denteneer, was shocked and took to Twitter to express her dismay, which went viral. The restaurant chain later stated that this service is typically free, but only when it is not explicitly stated as being charged.

1. North Korea's cargo ship, the Mu Du Bong, ran aground off the coast of Mexico in July and was seized by Mexican authorities due to alleged violations of United Nations sanctions by the ship's owner, North Korea's Ocean Maritime Management company.

2. Mexico defended this move, stating that it acted responsibly as a United Nations member state, and the detained vessel and crew are currently being held in Mexico, with the crew staying at a hotel in Tuxpan and regularly visiting the ship.

3. The ship's seizure follows a previous incident in 2013 when another North Korean ship, the Chong Chon Gang, was detained by Panama for carrying undeclared weaponry, including MiG fighter jets, anti-aircraft systems, and explosives, hidden under bags of sugar.

Prime Minister David Cameron plans to offer 600,000 additional free childcare places each year, aiming to reduce costs as a barrier to employment, particularly for second earners. The initiative is expected to cost £350 million and will provide 30 hours of childcare weekly, equivalent to £5,000 worth of savings for working families. The government hopes this will enable families to work an extra 78 days a year without additional childcare costs.

Manchester City's young squad consolidated a 3-0 first-leg lead against Leicester City with two late goals from Isaac Buckley and Brandon Barker at the King Power Stadium. Layton Ndukwu had earlier given Leicester hope with a penalty, but the efforts of City kept Leicester from clawing back the advantage. In the final, City will face Chelsea later this month, with the first leg at the City Football Academy Stadium on April 20, followed by the second leg at Stamford Bridge a week later.

Russian President Vladimir Putin downplayed the effects of Western sanctions on his country during an annual Q&A session, stating they were more about restraining Russia's development rather than specifically targeting Ukraine and Crimea. He defended the decision to lift sanctions on the sale of a sophisticated air defense system to Iran, claiming it encourages Iranian partners as part of a preliminary deal to limit Iran's nuclear program. Critics argue this annual event, characterized by extensive questions and responses, is a staged demonstration of democracy, rather than a true opportunity for the public to question their leader.

1. Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood will bring 22-year-old Gary Gardner, who enjoyed a successful loan spell at Nottingham Forest, back for pre-season training to evaluate his potential in the Premier League.

2. Gardner, a former England Under-21 player who was born in Solihull and joined Villa's academy at age seven, has expressed his desire to make an impact at the club having signed a new contract despite suffering serious knee injuries.

3. Gardner had a tremendous free-kick goal against Watford during his loan at Forest, and if he doesn't make it at Villa, he's keen on returning to Forest again for another loan spell, considering them his second club due to their support during his recovery.

A stampede occurred at a nightclub in Santiago, Chile, during a British punk band's performance, resulting in three fatalities and over a dozen injuries. The incident transpired as an equally large group attempted to force their way into the club, Tsunami, to see the band Doom, who were performing inside at the time. The police have arrested several individuals in connection to the tragedy, and the deceased individuals are thought to be in their 20s and 30s, with their identities yet to be officially confirmed. The band, Doom, is known for playing Crust Punk music.

Bayern Munich advanced to the semi-final of the German Cup after a 5-3 penalty shoot-out victory against Bayer Leverkusen, but Pep Guardiola expressed concern about his team's scoring form and the absence of Franck Ribery (ankle injury) and Arjen Robben (stomach muscle tear). Robben is out until May and Ribery's recovery is uncertain, leaving Bayern with a lack of options for one-on-one situations. Without the influential duo, Guardiola will look for solutions as Bayern hosts Eintracht Frankfurt in the Bundesliga this weekend, aiming to maintain their 10-point advantage over Wolfsburg. The only goal scored in Bayern's last three encounters came from Robert Lewandowski in a win against former club Borussia Dortmund, with Bayern set to face Dortmund again in the German Cup semi-final.

Derry Mathews' world title challenge is uncertain due to Richard Abril's withdrawal for the second time, threatening his second defense of the WBA lightweight belt initially scheduled for April 18 in Liverpool. Mathews may still contend for the title in Liverpool if the WBA strips Abril of his belt. Mathews secured a fifth-round knockout victory against Gyorgy Mezei Jnr in Liverpool on March 6, raising expectations for a future WBA title fight.

1. An English Bulldog named Hazel demonstrates exuberant curiosity by trying to conquer a washing basket, resulting in humorous mishaps like toppling the basket and tumbling out inside it, followed by chewing on the basket's rim.

2. The incident was captured on video and shows Hazel's playful nature, as she continues to explore various objects such as a skateboard, mirrors, and new collars in other videos shared on her owner's YouTube and Instagram channels.

3. Overall, Hazel's videos showcase the endless energy, curiosity, and unique antics that make her an adorable and entertaining puppy.

Catholic bishops in the U.S. have criticized the BBC drama "Wolf Hall" for its perceived anti-Catholic bias, particularly towards historical figures Thomas Cromwell and Sir Thomas More. The Catholic News Service described Cromwell as a "monster" and More as an "evidence-flouting caricature," while a reviewer from The Washington Post warned of ideological bias in the portrayal of historical facts. Despite these negative reviews, the series, starring Damian Lewis as King Henry VIII, was generally anticipated as a notable British import in U.S. media.

Today, victims of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting are set to receive Purple Heart medals, but some, like Staff Sergeant Shawn Manning, claim they have been denied crucial financial support. Manning was shot six times in the attack, but the Army has rejected his claims that his injuries were sustained in the line of duty, thereby denying him benefits under the 2015 National Defense Authorization Act. Notably, the attack was initially classified as workplace violence, but it was subsequently acknowledged as an act of terrorism inspired by a foreign terrorist group. The controversy originates from the Army's decision that victims of attacks inspired by foreign terrorist organizations are not eligible for combat benefits.

1. Newcastle United head coach John Carver believes he has the hardest job in football amidst supporter protests and poor on-field results.
2. The supporters are protesting against owner Mike Ashley's perceived lack of investment and ambition, as the club has reported record profits and has £34m sitting in a bank account.
3. Carver has urged the fans to attend the upcoming match against Spurs, expressing respect for their concerns but emphasizing the importance of supporting the team despite their dissatisfaction with the club's management.

Jordan Spieth, 21, won the 2015 Masters tournament at Augusta, becoming the first player to reach 19 under par in the event. He maintained a four-shot advantage throughout the final day, securing his victory with a final round of 70. Having finished second at the Masters in 2014, Spieth's win marks a significant accomplishment in his young career. Born in Dallas, Texas, Spieth gained attention as a teenager, winning two US Junior Amateur titles and making the cut at a PGA event at 17. He turned professional in 2012 and won the PGA Tour Rookie of the Year award that same year. Off the course, Spieth recently purchased a $2.3 million mansion in his hometown.

Beatrice Tollman, founder of a luxury hotel chain and a known Conservative donor, faced tax evasion charges in the past, although she was later acquitted. Her husband Stanley Tollman pleaded guilty to tax evasion but paid a substantial sum to the US government to resolve the matter. The Conservative Party, who has pledged to raise £5 billion from clamping down on tax avoidance, has stated they will return donations from the Tollmans following the revelation. This decision could potentially generate embarrassment for Prime Minister David Cameron, who has previously criticized aggressive tax avoidance.

The article discusses a complaint made by Poppy Smart, a marketing coordinator, against builders who allegedly sexually harassed her by wolf-whistling and making sexist comments during her daily commute. Despite initially choosing to ignore the unwanted attention, Smart felt increasingly upset and threatened following a month of the daily 'ritual'. She contacted the police and the construction company to report the incidents, likening the wolf-whistling to racial discrimination. The police treated the complaint as a potential anti-social behavior incident, with the construction company taking measures to address the issue. This issue highlights the persistent problem of street harassment, particularly wolf-whistling, which some deem to be a form of everyday sexism.

A UK teenager named Lily Sharp played a prank on her mother by faking her own kidnapping, referencing the film "Taken" in her texts. The prank involved convincing her mother that an intruder had entered their home and taken Lily's phone, demanding a ransom of £4000 for her return. Lily's mother became increasingly frantic, believing the intruder was holding her daughter captive. After revealing her location in a series of texts, Lily eventually admitted the prank, but her mother was not amused. Despite the upset, Lily's post about the prank received over 18,000 retweets and 25,000 favorites on Twitter.

On March 3, in the first one-day international in Dhaka, Bangladesh defeated Pakistan by 79 runs in a World Cup quarter-final rematch. Tamim Iqbal and Mushfiqur Rahim scored centuries, with Tamim making 132 and Mushfiqur scoring 106, to help Bangladesh reach 329 for six. Pakistan's response fell short at 250, with Wahab Riaz taking four wickets for 59 runs. The second ODI of the series will take place on March 6 in Mirpur.

Todd Kincannon, a 33-year-old Columbia attorney and former South Carolina Republican Party executive director, has been arrested and charged with criminal domestic violence, following an incident involving his wife, Ashley Griffith, on March 26. According to the arrest warrant, Kincannon allegedly grabbed Griffith's arm during an argument in their car and threatened to kill her, himself, and her family. After the incident, Griffith provided audio recordings and photographic evidence of verbal abuse and possible domestic violence to FITS. Kincannon claims the incident was triggered by an overdose on the prescription drug Benzonatate, and has previously been recognized for sending inflammatory tweets, including a tweet in September 2014 about Ray Rice's domestic violence incident that was considered by many as offensive and insensitive. After his recent arrest, Kincannon has reportedly deleted his Twitter account.

Jordan Spieth, fresh from winning the Masters and breaking Tiger Woods' record, is participating in the RBC Heritage Classic this week despite a busy media schedule. He arrives having completed 26 appearances and interviews in 25 hours. Spieth, aiming to surpass Rory McIlroy as the world's top golfer, believes the success won't change him and is committed to playing in this tournament. Known for previous success at Sea Pines Resort, where he finished ninth in 2013 and 12th last year, Spieth will attempt to compete despite not having practiced on the course before the tournament's first round. The RBC Heritage has been significant for Spieth's career, providing job security and a top-10 finish in 2012, and he looks forward to playing this week.

Samantha Cameron, a former British Prime Minister David Cameron's wife, revealed her fondness for the alternative band Poliça, known for their psychedelic rock and radical feminist inspirations. The band's music, often containing violent and sexual imagery, contrasts starkly with Mrs. Cameron's aristocratic background and traditional upbringing. Samantha Cameron attended a Poliça gig in Shoreditch, East London, to show her support for the band.

The Australian government plans to impose a 10% goods and services tax (GST) on movie and music downloads from streaming services like Netflix and Apple, potentially extending to online purchases from overseas companies below A$1,000. This proposed change aims to boost GST revenue. While it may affect companies such as Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and eBay, consumer advocacy group Choice suggests that tech-savvy Australians might evade the tax through the use of virtual private networks (VPNs).

ESPN's Stephen A. Smith is facing criticism for his stance on boxer Floyd Mayweather Jr., who has a history of domestic violence convictions. Smith suggested that Mayweather's boxing career should be considered separately from his violent history, and when co-host Cari Champion disagreed, Smith implied that her opinion was influenced by her gender. The upcoming fight between Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao has stirred debates, with Pacquiao's trainer positioning Pacquiao as the 'good' figure and Mayweather as 'evil.'

A 12-year-old boy named Mahendra Ahirwar from Madhya Pradesh, India, suffers from a rare condition that causes his head to hang at a 180-degree angle, limiting his ability to stand, walk, eat, or use the toilet independently. His parents, Mukesh and Sumitra Ahirwar, have consulted over 50 doctors across India but have yet to receive a diagnosis. Despite their efforts, the family has been met with community blame for Mahendra's condition and discrimination. His mother, Sumitra, has expressed her desperation, stating, "I cannot see him suffer anymore... He cannot do anything by himself. He just sits in a corner of the room all day. It's no life." Although they have exhausted medical resources, the family remains hopeful and continues to seek a cure for Mahendra.

The 2015 World Happiness Report revealed Switzerland as the world's happiest nation, with strong economic growth, social bonds, and increasing life expectancy as key contributors. Iceland, known for its breathtaking scenery and rich cultural history, climbed to the second spot on the list. Nick Clegg, the Liberal Democrat leader, has been accused of deflecting responsibility for his party's poor poll ratings, instead blaming various groups for deserting the party since 2010. Camellias are versatile, evergreen shrubs known for their bright flowers that contrast well with glossy leaves. They thrive in acid, free-draining, and nutrient-rich soil, but are sensitive to alkaline or neutral soil. If soil is unsuitable, they can be grown in containers with ericaceous compost. Camellias are hardy and can be pruned for various aesthetics, from wall-trained to hedges. They flower from winter to spring, with many varieties boasting extended bloom periods. Potted camellias have a shorter lifespan, but can be easily propagated through root cuttings. Popular camellia varieties include Donation, Adolphe Audusson, Alba Simplex, and St Ewe, each offering unique bloom colors and seasons. Proper care includes preventing premature bud drop, addressing magnesium deficiencies, and managing dead flower debris.

The article features the greater adjutant stork, a majestic and intelligent bird species, which thrives in the Boragaon landfill in Guwahati, India. This landfill, roughly 94 acres and surrounded by swamplands, is home to around 100 families, who scavenge for valuable materials like plastic, metal, and wires to sell and live in self-constructed homes made from recycled materials. Despite the challenging and unhygienic conditions, photographer Timothy Bouldry, who has visited landfills worldwide for seven years, describes the community as content, hopeful, and spiritually connected. Bouldry has made it his mission to support the people living in landfills, using his photography to highlight their resilience and learning new skills such as cultivating gardens and teaching English classes.

A study conducted at the University of Reading found that chewing gum helps reduce the occurrence and intensity of earworms, or catchy songs that persistently lodge in one's mind. The volunteers in the study were less likely to think about and "hear" the songs in their minds when chewing gum. This effect suggests that the same technique could potentially help manage other unwanted or intrusive thoughts, such as those associated with obsessive-compulsive disorders. A British nuclear submarine, HMS Talent, suffered £500,000 in damage after colliding with a floating ice patch while tracking Russian vessels, according to The Mail on Sunday. The incident occurred last year, and the submarine is currently out of action for several months for repairs. The incident occurred during heightened tensions between Britain and Russia in the North Sea and Arctic Circle regions, with Russia increasing its submarine activity by 50% in the past 18 months. The Royal Navy is investigating the collision and has stated that the damage is consistent with striking an object while surfacing, although they refuse to disclose exact details of the collision. The damage Devastated the submarine's outer layer of acoustic tiles, which minimize the transmission of sound waves and other signals that could reveal the submarine's position. The Royal Navy has previously used the "hitting ice" explanation to explain similar damages caused by enemy vessels during the Cold War.

A study has found that consuming two cups of coffee daily could potentially reduce the risk of breast cancer recurrence by half in women undergoing hormonal therapy (tamoxifen) after treatment. The study suggests this could be due to coffee's influence on breast cancer cells, causing them to divide less frequently and die more often, particularly when combined with tamoxifen. This is not the first study to link coffee consumption with improved cancer prognosis; previous research has indicated it may also reduce the risk of liver and skin cancers.

Authorities in greater Sydney, Australia are planning to control a observed surge in the population of wild rabbits, considered a pest, through a program of strategically placing carrots laced with the Calicivirus, also known as Rabbit haemorrhagic disease (RHD). This virus, which kills up to 100% of infected rabbits, is aimed at reducing the population to prevent damage to agriculture, environment, and native wildlife. The program has been implemented annually for nine years and is planned to take place in May in select areas, with additional measures planned for areas where the population reduction has been insufficient. Pet owners of domestic rabbits are being urged to vaccinate their rabbits to protect them against the virus. The rabbits were introduced to Australia by the British settlers and reproduce rapidly.
