The Augusta National Golf Club has implemented a cell phone ban during the Masters tournament, prompting fans to revive old cameras, such as digital and 35mm models, for capturing photos of golfers like Tiger Woods. Many are re-learning camera basics and are using the equipment for the first time at Augusta, while others are experienced photographers with specific targets, like favorite players or scenic locations. The ban produced humorous moments, particularly when fans struggled with vintage cameras or attempted to take selfies with point-and-shoot devices. Despite the inconvenience, some fans enjoyed reliving the old-school experience by creating physical photo albums and framed prints.

Allie Davis, a 21-year-old woman from Minneapolis, created a pop culture trivia test for her boyfriend, focusing primarily on Beyonce's music, to maintain their relationship. He scored 80%. She shared the results on Twitter, also including questions about other artists, like One Direction. While many considered the test a humorous stunt, one commentator suggested it was a warning sign, to which Allie responded it was a lighthearted joke.

Ocean photographer Lloyd Meudell captures the surreal moment when ocean foam explodes in the air, creating dream-like images reminiscent of surrealist works like those by Salvador Dali. He primarily takes these shots on Kiama and Gerrigong beaches along the south coast of New South Wales, using an EOS 5D Mark III DSLR and numerous lenses. To budding photographers, Meudell advises familiarizing oneself with how the ocean works, citing experience with surfing as particularly useful for this type of photography, and suggests starting with a GoPro before moving to a DSLR.

Bayern Munich manager Pep Guardiola blames injuries for the team's Champions League quarter-final first-leg defeat by Porto, who took a 2-0 lead after early goals from Ricardo Quaresma and Jackson Martinez, with a second-half effort from Martinez. Porto manager Julen Lopetegui expresses hope for a semi-final spot, urging his team to be "perfect" in the second leg. Martinez, returning from injury, scored two goals and troubled Bayern's defenders throughout the match. Quaresma also praised Porto's team ethic for their victory.

The Curiosity Rover has discovered multi-colored, mineral veins on Mars, located at a site called 'Garden City' on the slopes of Mount Sharp. These veins, ranging from 2.5 inches tall, are believed to have formed from fluids moving through cracked rock during Mars' wet past, with both bright and dark materials present. Scientists believe these veins provide insights into Mars' watery past, suggesting the planet once had more water than the Arctic Ocean and the water remained for over 1.5 billion years, potentially providing ample conditions for life on Mars. The findings also indicate that Mars has lost 87% of its original water over the last 3.7 billion years, leaving it dry and barren today. The study is the first to determine the exact amount of water Mars had in its past.

A 25-year-old man named Carl Bradey sustained severe burns on his entire body after rescuing a three-year-old girl from a house fire caused by a candle in his rental property. The incident left Bradey with nerve damage in his right arm and unable to feel anything. He is currently staying with his mother, recovering from multiple surgeries including skin grafts and vein removal. His family has set up a crowdfunding page to support Bradey's recovery efforts. Fire safety experts advise using candles in solid holders away from flammable materials. The house has since been demolished due to asbestos found in the property.

The accidentally introduced bacterium Xylella fastidiosa is causing the death of thousands of olive trees in southern Italy's Puglia region, affecting a third of the national olive crop and leading to a 35% production decline. Italian authorities are taking drastic measures to halt the spread by felling and burning infected olive groves, which, while causing local protests, is necessary according to EU Food Safety Commissioner Vytenis Andriukaitis. This destruction is likely to lead to olive oil shortages and higher prices globally, particularly in Britain. The largest olive oil export markets for Italy are the USA, Canada, China, Japan, Hong Kong, India, Russia, and Singapore.

A border guard was killed and ten others injured in a cross-fire incident with militants at the Saudi-Yemen border, marking the first known military death for Saudi Arabia since launching airstrikes against rebels in Yemen. Houthi rebels seized the presidential palace in Aden, a city in southern Yemen, and have control of most large districts there amid ongoing clashes. U.S. Navy warships are patrolling off Yemen to search for suspicious shipping, particularly any weapons shipments from Iran to the Houthi rebels, but a Panamanian-registered cargo ship was found to be carrying only cement and construction materials.

A 53-year-old man named Muhammed Tahir was convicted of sexual assault after rubbing himself inappropriately on a young woman on the London Underground. The incident, which was witnessed by undercover police officers, left the victim "frightened and shocking". Despite the judge stating there should be a custodial sentence, Tahir received a six-month prison sentence suspended for two years, a 12-month supervision order, 150 hours of unpaid work, an £80 victim surcharge, and a ban from using the London Underground during rush hours for five years.

A Californian man, Robin Barton, met the retired Santa Ana police officer, Michael Buelna, who saved his life 25 years ago when he was abandoned as an infant behind a dumpster. Despite Buelna initially wanting to adopt Barton, his adoptive parents, Elizabeth Barton and Daniel Fernandez, claimed him. Both sides were emotional to meet, as they share a bond due to Buelna also being abandoned as a child. Barton expressed his gratitude to Buelna and also expressed a desire to find his biological mother for closure.

A 16-year-old student named Courtney Brain was given a detention for missing half an hour of lessons due to an emergency appointment with her GP for a water infection. Her mother, Jane Burnham, criticized the school, Skegness Academy, for being petty and unreasonable. The school claimed the detention was to give Courtney the best chance for her upcoming exams, but Courtney's mother contested that the detention would not significantly impact her grades and noted Courtney's excellent attendance record.

Graeme Finlay, a 53-year-old former naval serviceman, was acquitted of assaulting two elderly passengers on a cruise ship after an incident over insults at a dinner table. He claimed self-defense after being hit by one of the victims, who was using a crutch, and the jury at Teesside Crown Court found him not guilty of unlawful wounding and inflicting grievous bodily harm in less than an hour. Finlay expressed relief and regret over the disturbing ordeal that left the couple with injuries.

Hayley Carney, a transgender woman living in the U.S., is planning to move to the UK to marry her unidentified fiancée, Anne, who resides in Plymouth, Devon. Carney aims to become a British citizen and fulfil a lifelong dream, believing the UK is more accepting of her identity. She will undergo gender transition surgery before the move and will apply for a marriage visa after arrival, setting her on the path to citizenship. Carney chose the UK because of her childhood fascination with the country and acknowledges the kindness and acceptance of British people. She intends to find employment upon arrival and is prepared to go through the proper immigration channels to achieve British citizenship.

1. Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone has expressed surprise at the absence of English clubs in the Champions League quarter-finals this season, with Chelsea, Arsenal, Manchester City, and Everton previously eliminated.

2. Simeone, who leads Atletico against local rivals Real Madrid in the second leg of their quarter-final, believes the poor performance of English teams is a wake-up call for the Premier League.

3. Despite his shock at the plight of Premier League clubs, Simeone maintains that Spain still houses the two best teams in Europe, with Real Madrid and Barcelona potentially facing Atletico in the semi-finals. The Real-Atletico tie remains evenly poised following a 0-0 draw in the first leg.

David Cameron and Boris Johnson, aiming to promote Tory plans for expanded childcare, struggled with a children's seasonal jigsaw puzzle at a day nursery in Surbiton. The puzzle proved more challenging than anticipated, with Boris Johnson attempting to force pieces together and proposing the slogan, "If in doubt, wedge it in." After a young child pointed out several errors, the pair found success in a finger painting activity. The incident sparked humor and comparisons to their election campaign, with David Cameron stating afterwards, "That was a bit like the (election) campaign... suddenly, the final surge."

Justice Diana Bryant, a top judge in Brisbane, proposes the regulation and legalization of commercial surrogacy in Australia to prevent instances of child abandonment, particularly in the light of recent cases like Baby Gammy. She believes that this move would allow for ethical regulation of surrogacy, prevent parents from entering into unlawful arrangements overseas, and ensure that surrogate children in Australia have the opportunity to know their biological parents.

A seven-storey fall survivor, aptly named 'Seven', has been on the road to recovery at My Vet Animal Hospital after being found injured and covered in maggots in Zetland, inner-east of Sydney. 'Seven' sustained serious injuries, including a broken jaw, broken leg, broken hard palate, and bruised lungs. The cat's story of survival captivated the hearts of many who donated funds to help pay for his medical expenses. After receiving two surgeries, costing over $3000, Seven is now learning to walk again and will be ready for a new home in about six weeks.

MasterChef UK crowned its eleventh series winner, Simon Wood, a data manager from Oldham, Greater Manchester, who impressed judges John Torode and Gregg Wallace with his innovative three-course meal. Wood's victory marks a dream come true as he has aspired to become a chef since he was eight years old. Meanwhile, Kim Woodward, a former MasterChef semi-finalist, made history by becoming the first woman to head the kitchen at the prestigious Savoy Grill in London, with its iconic dishes attracting numerous high-profile guests for over a century. Woodward returned to the Savoy Grill following her tenure at York & Albany in Camden.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce acknowledges the need for 'crazy results' to preserve their Premier League status, as they prepare to face Southampton with only a two-point cushion above the relegation zone. The unpredictable nature of the season is highlighted, with meetings still to come against high-profile teams like Liverpool, Arsenal, and Manchester United. Bruce is confronted with a decision about the form of goalkeeper Allan McGregor, who has recently committed high-profile blunders, with veteran Steve Harper and Tom Huddlestone lining up for a potential return. Bruce rates Southampton, who are managed by Ronald Koeman, highly, making the upcoming game a significant challenge for the Tigers.

Celebrity chef Bobby Flay is reportedly offering his ex-wife, actress Stephanie March, a monthly sum of $5,000 as per their prenup, despite his net worth exceeding $20 million. The prenup also stipulates that he can buy out the $8 million marital home for $1 million, with an additional $50,000 for moving expenses. March is reportedly dissatisfied with this arrangement. The couple, known for their ten-year marriage that ended recently, are in the process of divorce, with no issues regarding child support due to the lack of children. The marriage is said to have deteriorated over the past year and a half, with a turning point being when Flay did not visit March in the hospital after her appendix burst. Bobby Flay has been in two previous marriages, and this will be Stephanie March's first divorce. There have been rumors of a romantic involvement between Flay and fellow chef Giada De Laurentiis, which both parties have since denied.

Leading Australian modeling agencies are now focusing on 'insta-fame' as a new criterion for models, with the rise of social media necessitating the addition of 'influencer' and 'blogger' divisions to their traditional model portfolios. These divisions cater to the growing demand from clients for models with high social media followings, alongside conventional requirements of beauty, fitness, and health. Agencies are increasingly seeking models with substantial online presence, with client expectations ranging from as little as 10,000 to upwards of 300,000 followers. This blend of a desirable 'cool girl' image and a substantial social media following is seen as a lucrative combination for businesses seeking rapid brand promotion and increased visibility.

Hungarian architect Matyas Gutai and his collaborator Milan Berenyi have built a prototype house using a "liquid engineering" system in Kecskemet, Hungary. This innovative design involves trapping a sheet of water between inner layers of the house's structure, which self-regulates temperature and can reheat itself through excess heat storage. The house, showcased with a grant from the EU, is more efficient, sustainable, and can generate its own energy, potentially reducing carbon emissions. Gutai developed this concept after observing the heat retention of water in open-air hot baths during a trip to the University of Tokyo. To address potential issues, such as freezing temperatures or panel breaks, the water is mixed with non-polluting solvents and the structure is insulated for colder climates, while special joint units are designed to accommodate panel failure. This technology, while moderately more expensive, aims to significantly reduce energy needs as an approach towards making cities more independent of energy suppliers and building a greener future.

Cardiff City have returned their allocation of 500 tickets for the Championship game against Leeds United at Elland Road, citing a desire to support a fan-led boycott campaign. This decision follows Leeds' initial offer of only 500 tickets without travel restrictions to Cardiff fans, compared to the 2,200 tickets they offered Cardiff fans for the reverse fixture at the Cardiff City Stadium. The absence of Cardiff supporters will result in an unusually silent Elland Road during the game on Saturday. Cardiff CEO Ken Choo and the club's Supporters Club have expressed disappointment and frustration over the situation, and have criticized West Yorkshire Police for their perceived heavy-handed treatment of away fans.

Utah photographer Alan Lawrence, after initially feeling negative emotions upon learning that his newborn son Wil had Down Syndrome, now finds that Wil brings joy to the family and has opened new opportunities. Lawrence created a photo series called 'Wil Can Fly' to depict Wil as flying in various scenes, raising awareness about Down Syndrome. The father, inspired by Wil's natural instinct to 'fly,' aims to continue capturing Wil in flight, donating half the proceeds from a calendar and Kickstarter campaign to Down Syndrome foundations.

In February 2012, a stadium riot between supporters of Egyptian football teams Al-Masry and Al-Ahly in Port Said resulted in 74 deaths, sparking further violence in Cairo, leading to 16 more deaths. An appeals court ordered a retrial of 73 defendants, including fans, police officers, and club officials, after rejecting an initial verdict that sentenced 21 people to death. Today, the court upheld the death sentences for 11 of the football fans, with their final decision being made on May 30 by Egypt's supreme court. The incident was the deadliest stadium riot in Egypt's history, where football fans frequently clash with rival supporters and security forces. Other recent incidents involving fan violence include a stampede at a Cairo stadium that resulted in 22 deaths this year, and ongoing clashes with police, who have accused Islamist groups of causing the unrest.

In the Ghanaian slum of Nima, a local mosque provides a venue for weekly coding classes for young girls, led by tech entrepreneur Regina Agyare. This initiative, part of Agyare's mentorship program "Tech Needs Girls," aims to empower these girls, many of whom face social barriers to education, and give them a voice through technology. The classes have been well-received by the community, despite initial resistance, and are now an integral part of Achievers Ghana, a non-profit organization that supports the education of local girls. Agyare's goal is not to turn every girl into a software developer, but to help them reach their full potential and bring positive change to their community.

The Wisconsin church's four-decade tradition of mud-wrestling pigs at a summer fundraiser, known as the Original Pig Rassle, has been cancelled due to allegations of animal cruelty. The Global Conservation Group, an animal advocacy group, launched an online petition claiming the tournament was inhumane to the pigs, which garnered over 81,000 signatures. In response, St Patrick's Parish in Stephensville has announced that the event will be replaced this August with a human mud foosball tournament. The church's decision to discontinue the Original Pig Rassle is being considered a victory for animal welfare by the Global Conservation Group.

Tennis players Maria Sharapova and Venus Williams have withdrawn from their countries' Fed Cup ties due to a leg injury for Sharapova and personal reasons for Williams. Sharapova was unable to participate in Russia's semi-final against Germany in Sochi and there is a question mark over her participation in the WTA Stuttgart Open. Venus Williams will be replaced by Lauren Davis in the USA's World Group play-off against Italy, with Serena Williams leading the American team on red clay.

A 36-year-old woman from Gary, Indiana, suspected of posing as a Child Protective Services employee, has been taken into police custody on suspicion of kidnapping and murdering a 23-year-old mother, Samantha Fleming, in Anderson, Indiana, with the intent to steal Fleming's three-week-old daughter, Serenity. Fleming's body was found in Gary, wrapped in plastic and doused with bleach on Friday. Remarkably, the baby has been found and is safe. The suspect is under mental health care in a Texas hospital and has not yet had any charges filed. The baby will be returned to relatives in Anderson following the tragic event.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, worked at the same call-center company and lived only six minutes away after the Ohio Department of Heath released birth records. Upon receiving her records, Mitchell-Clark found Simmons on Facebook, connected with her, and they eventually decided to meet. Simmons also has three biological daughters, two of whom, Kamala and Maisha Cummings, expressed relief and joy upon meeting Mitchell-Clark. Mitchell-Clark's adoptive parents have been supportive of her search for her biological parents.

An Icelandic duo has created a protein-rich energy bar named Jungle Bar, which includes cricket flour as a major ingredient. Claimed to be a good source of protein and other essential nutrients, the bar is also free from gluten, peanuts, dairy, and soy. The creators hope their product will encourage western diets to incorporate more insect-based food to address nutritional needs and reduce environmental impact. The Jungle Bar is currently seeking funding on Kickstarter for further production, with a planned shipping start in August 2015.

A 73-year-old reserve deputy, Robert Charles Bates, mistook his pistol for a stun gun during an undercover drug operation and fatally shot 44-year-old Eric Courtney Harris. Harris was attempting to sell a 9mm semi-automatic pistol to undercover officers, with police claiming he reached for his waistband causing deputies to believe he was a threat. Bates, who is classified as an advanced deputy, has been a reserve since 2008 and is the CEO of Robert C Bates LLC, a Tulsa-based insurance company. He had previously worked as a full-time officer and with the Tulsa Police Auxiliary.

On May 5-7, an unmanned Russian spacecraft called Progress 59, which lost contact with flight controllers during a resupply mission to the International Space Station (ISS), will re-enter Earth's atmosphere. This event will not pose a threat to the ISS as its orbit is significantly different, according to Roscosmos, the Russian Federal Space Agency. The cargo spacecraft was carrying over 3 tons of supplies for the ISS, but these were non-critical for the U.S. Operating Segment of the station. Russian flight controllers are continuing their efforts to make contact with Progress 59 as it passes over Russian ground stations.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce has revealed that players will face up to a 50% salary reduction if the team is relegated, due to financial provisions set up in their contracts. The team is currently in 17th place with a tough run-in ahead, and their wage bill is the third-lowest in the Premier League. Bruce is hoping for a recovery from midfielder Mo Diame, who has been out with a knee injury, as they aim to avoid relegation and prevent a financial struggle similar to the one the club faced before the current owners took over. Bruce commended the job done by Crystal Palace's managers Alan Pardew and Tony Pulis at Selhurst Park.

Leo Schofield, a 79-year-old restaurant critic and festival curator, expressed feelings of bitterness and depression about his decade living in Tasmania, stating it was the unhappiest time of his life. He initially moved to the state to establish a Baroque music festival but ended up relocating to New South Wales after the Tasmanian Government reduced funding for the festival. Schofield, who now plans to reserve a chapter in his memoirs titled 'Revenge of the Bogans' to discuss his Tasmanian experience, has observed Tasmania as a state filled with 'dregs, bogans, and third-generation morons', comments that drew criticism from Luke Martin, a representative from the Tourism Industry Council of Tasmania.

The photography competition held by the Northern Territory Cattlemen's Association annually showcases the unique outback lifestyle, people, and landscapes of regional Australia. The competition, hosted during the association's conference, highlights the challenges and connections in rural life, particularly the bond between humans and animals. Marie Muldoon won this year's competition with a touching photo of her daughter cuddling a horse, titled "True Love," while the best landscape photograph, "No.11 Ammaroo," showcasing waterlogged farmland, was awarded to Anna Weir. The competition has previously recognized Jacynta Coffey for emblematic shots like "Trucking," which represents typical station life, and "Feeding the Bulls," a moving photo of a child amidst rushing bulls.

The book "Sex by Numbers" explores various sexual statistical claims to separate myths from realities, focusing on penis size measurements. The latest study, involving 15,521 penis measurements from worldwide participants, indicates that the average erect penis size is approximately 5.2 inches in length with a 4.6-inch circumference, with the most accurate measurements being made by trained health professionals. The book also discusses other sexual statistics such as the average time between penetration and ejaculation (nine minutes for heterosexual couples), the effects of physical exercise and baldness on sexual functioning, and the myth that bigger body parts indicate a larger penis. The book challenges common beliefs and offers insights on what truly contributes to great sex.

Barnet Football Club returned to the Football League after a two-year absence following a 2-0 win against Gateshead in the Conference clash. Two goals from Mauro Vilhete sealed the promotion, with the second crushing any hope of a comeback from Gateshead. The victory marked Martin Allen's fourth spell in charge as the most successful. Gateshead put up a fight but were continually on the back foot, managing to threaten the champions only minimally on this finale day. Barnet clinched the Conference title, securing promotion, while relegation was confirmed for Alfreton, Telford United, Dartford, and Nuneaton.

Remains of a missing college freshler, Anjelica 'AJ' Hadsell, 18, have been found 40 miles from her home in Norfolk, Virginia. The remains were found outside a residence in Franklin and have been sent to the Chief Medical Examiner's Office for identification and to determine cause of death. Investigations including the FBI are ongoing, with no evidence of foul play initially reported, but concerns among family and friends persist as Hadsell vanished on purpose. Hadsell's stepfather, Wesley Hadsell, was arrested for breaking into a home, claimed to be in search of AJ. He has a history of criminal offenses, including a past case of kidnapping and driving across multiple states, for which charges were dropped.

The article discusses rumors that Apple plans to address the 'bend gate' issue with the iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus by using stronger materials for its next generation smartphones. This may include the use of 7000 series aluminum, a material used in competition bicycles and the Apple Watch Sport edition. This alloy is said to be 60% harder than standard alloys. The upcoming iPhones, expected to be called the iPhone 6S and iPhone 6S Plus, may also include the A9 chip, Force Touch Feature, and a possible four-inch version called the iPhone 6C. The article cautions users to avoid putting excessive pressure on the middle of the phone to prevent bending.

1. English rugby teams have struggled in European competitions recently, with English clubs not winning the top prize since 2007. This year's Champions Cup does not seem to be the year to break this cycle, as bookmakers predict that holders Toulon will win for the third consecutive year, with Clermont as their main contenders.

2. Despite the presence of four English sides in the last eight, they are all underdogs this weekend, facing challenging away matches against well-established European teams. English teams have historically struggled in French territory, losing all but one away quarter-final against French opposition.

3. However, some English teams, such as Bath and Saracens, are still considered contenders. A successful run in the Champions Cup would provide a significant boost to England's morale, particularly in the World Cup year, but it will be a challenging task given the significant financial resources and international talent possessed by many European teams.

A New York-based teacher named Sam Pearce, who initially moved to the city to teach English, was discovered as a model on the subway and now works for top fashion designers. Despite juggling both jobs, Mr. Pearce insists that his teaching responsibilities are his priority, and his agents have accommodated his school schedule. He has used his newfound fame to raise funds for his students by launching a Go-Fund-Me campaign and is urging donors to support teachers and students through DonorsChoose.org.

An amateur astronomer, Gordon Ewen, captured a unique image of a sun spot that resembles a chick sitting on the sun's surface. Sun spots are cooler regions on the sun's surface caused by concentrations of magnetic fields and can be seen from Earth without a telescope. They range in size, sometimes being more than ten times larger than Earth, and are often the source of solar eruptions like flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs). Gordon Ewen, a retired chemist from Hertfordshire, took the photograph using a telescope in his garden shed, which he set up after leaving his job five years ago due to his lifelong interest in astronomy. The misleading image of a sun spot in the article was not a sun spot.

Vladimir Putin is allegedly planning to utilize the threat of nuclear war to defend the Crimean peninsula from being reclaimed by Ukraine and potentially expanding Russian control into NATO's border countries, with imminent actions thought to involve cyber attacks or ethnic tensions in the Baltic states. Russia perceives NATO's military presence in the Baltics as an encroachment and has reportedly issued a range of responses, including nuclear, to this perceived threat. The ongoing conflict in eastern Ukraine and any future attempt to return Crimea to Ukraine are identified as potential flashpoints for nuclear war between Russia and the West.

Virgin Galactic aims to test a new version of SpaceShipTwo by the end of the year, following the crash of its predecessor in the Mojave Desert in 2014. The company plans to apply lessons from the crash to enhance the performance of the new spacecraft. Chief executive George Whitesides stated that the spacecraft is nearly ready for test flights. The new SpaceShipTwo, if successful, will offer a sub-orbital space travel experience to paying customers at a starting price of £150,000 ($250,000). The aircraft will carry six passengers and two pilots, with each passenger having their own seating position with two large windows. The test flights will include ground and flight tests, with the exact timing dependent on safety and readiness. The previous SpaceShipTwo disintegrated in 2014 due to the accidental deployment of the 'feathering system' at an incorrect moment, resulting in the death of co-pilot Michael Alsbury and serious injuries to pilot Peter Siebold. A refugee couple in Cloverdale, Perth, claim their children are asking if they are "really monkeys" following a racially charged attack by a neighbor. Footage of the incident shows the woman allegedly attacking the men with a crowbar, using racist slurs like "monkeys" and "jungle n*****." Police have charged the woman with multiple offenses, but she maintains she was the victim. The family, from Congo, is shaken by the attack, with the father, Tumaini Eliazery, stating the incident has caused a negative impact on his family. The 51-year-old woman, a chef, insists she was in fear for her life during the encounter and believes the family should not be in Australia. She is set to appear in Perth Magistrates Court on April 8, facing charges of assault, disorderly conduct, going armed in public, and racially harassing conduct.

Walmart is under scrutiny after a stolen rifle from their Tuscon, Arizona store was used in a shooting incident by thief Mario Valencia. The weapon should have been locked but was found with a loose wire upon recovery, allowing it to be fired. A police officer, Officer Michael Rapiejko, used his vehicle to apprehend Valencia, who was later hospitalized and charged with several felonies for an alleged crime spree involving theft, vandalism, burglary, home invasion, and car theft. Officer Rapiejko was reinstated after an investigation cleared him of any wrongdoing in the incident.

A father-of-five, identified as Peter Kelly, was fatally stabbed following a three-hour verbal altercation with three other fishermen at the St Croix River in Wisconsin. Kelly and his friend, on the Minnesota side, asked the rowdy fishermen to quieten down, but the challenge was issued, and the argument escalated. After exchanging heated words, the three attackers arrived at the Wisconsin side where Kelly was stabbed, and they fled the scene after the crime. Authorities are still searching for the attackers, believed to be in their late teens or early 20s, who were traveling in two vehicles with Minnesota license plates. The small community of St Croix Falls is mourning the loss of Kelly, a high school volunteer coach, who leaves behind a loving wife and four sons, all under nine years old.

Holly Willoughby and Davina McCall, two popular presenters often referred to as "television's golden girls," have teamed up for their first campaign with Garnier Nutrisse. In the campaign, they celebrate finding their perfect hair shades and show off their glossy locks in a playful shoot, including posing with moustaches made from their hair. Holly has chosen Garnier Nutrisse 10.01 as her perfect multi-tonal blonde, while Davina prefers 4.3, a shade that matches her 60% grey hair which she needs to dye every three to four weeks. Recently, Holly also released a vintage-inspired baby clothing line, and Designing a range of vintage-inspired clothes for babies. Meanwhile, Davina renewed her wedding vows with her partner Matthew Robertson in Las Vegas.

The baby boomer generation's approaching mortality is anticipated to result in a surge of funeral debt, as a rising number of deaths and increasing funeral costs collide with financial pressures already faced by younger generations. The International Longevity Centre-UK's report predicts a 20% increase in deaths over the next two decades, and current funeral expenses have grown by 80% over the past decade, with a 'simple' funeral now costing around £3,590. These costs are increasing due to factors such as crematoria removal fees for mercury, rise in undertaker bills, and church fees. As a result, many households with limited savings could struggle to cover funeral expenses.

The Transportation Security Administration's Aviation Security Advisory Committee found that nationwide full screening of airport employees would not significantly lower overall public risk due to its inability to determine a person's intent to cause harm. Instead, the report advised a risk-based, multi-layered security approach that includes strengthening employee vetting, expanding the collection of domestic intelligence, and enhancing criminal background checks. Following the arrest of two airport workers for alleged gun smuggling in December, TSA Secretary Jeh Johnson announced immediate actions to address these recommendations.

Raheem Sterling and Jordon Ibe were pictured smoking a shisha pipe, an incident similar to past controversies by other Premier League stars. Jack Wilshere of Arsenal is one such star, having been involved in smoking controversies, including being photographed with a cigarette outside a London nightclub, smoking in a swimming pool in Las Vegas, and holding a shisha pipe during a night out in London. Diego Maradona, the Argentina's World Cup-winning captain, was suspended for substance abuse-related issues during his career, including a 15-month ban for cocaine and ephedrine use. Saido Berahino, the West Brom striker, was caught on camera inhaling a legal substance called 'hippy crack' while driving, leading to a drink-driving charge and a year-long driving ban. Kyle Walker, Spurs and England defender, also faced criticism for being pictured inhaling 'hippy crack' during a night out in Sheffield. The article discusses a new Reddit thread where members of the disabled community shared experiences of well-intended but offensive behavior from able-bodied people. Topics include being labeled as an inspiration, being praised for doing normal activities, unsolicited help, people taking control of their wheelchairs, accusations of faking disabilities, and suggesting treatments or cures. The most common complaint was being infantilized, and the thread advises against offering unsolicited help, recommending treatments, or bringing up religion in conversations with disabled individuals.

A German engineering team has developed a concept car named EOssc2, modeled after crabs to navigate tight urban parking spaces. The EOssc2 can turn on the spot, shrink in size, and move sideways. It is designed to be semi-autonomous, with a top speed of 40 mph and equipped with a 360-degree LIDAR sensor for navigation. The car is currently being tested in Bremen, Germany, and Dalian, China, with the goal of eventually creating a driverless car.

Middlesbrough secured a 2-0 home win over Rotherham United, with goals from Lee Tomlin and Patrick Bamford, keeping their automatic promotion hopes alive. The home side dominated the game, with Bamford scoring the opener in the second half and missing a late penalty, while Tomlin, Kike, and Emilio Nsue had chances to add to the scoreline. Despite the victory, Boro remained fourth in the Sky Bet Championship table due to wins by other top teams.

The Tewksbury Police Department in Massachusetts was targeted by hackers using the CryptoLocker malware, which encrypted vital records on their computer network. The department was forced to pay a $500 ransom in Bitcoin to restore access to their data, as the most recent back-up was corrupted. This observed incident of ransomware attack is not a data breach, as the information remains within the department's control, but the malware prevents it from being readable. The Tewksbury Police Department is just one of several police departments in the U.S. that have been victims of such attacks.

A Chinese woman named Zhu Diandian, whose surname translates to "pig" in Mandarin, has gained internet fame for her unique bond with her 187lb pet pig, Five Flowers. The pair sleep together, and Zhu often posts photos of them on social media, including selfies of her in bed with the pig. Her pet dog, not fond of this arrangement, is often kept out of the bedroom by a baby gate. Zhu's husband is reportedly tolerant of the relationship, and her pet pig is dressed and walked like a pet dog. Her social media posts have garnered thousands of comments and likes, with many netizens finding the bond between woman and pig endearing.

A woman, Louise Smith, secretly pulled two hairs from a young girl's head and planted them in her food at the Crown and Thistle pub in Cumbria, intending to get the meal for free as she couldn't afford the £21 bill. Smith was convicted of fraud in her absence at Carlisle Magistrates' Court this week. The pub has stated that they prioritize food hygiene and child protection, and an arrest warrant has been issued for Smith, who is now on the run.

Thailand's Kiradech Aphibarnrat won the inaugural Shenzhen International, claiming his second European Tour title in a play-off. Aphibarnrat trailed Li Hao-tong by two shots with two holes left, but an eagle on the 17th and a missed birdie chance on the last took the match to extra holes. Aphibarnrat then holed a birdie putt in the play-off to secure victory, with Li missing from long range. Aphibarnrat, who had a tough year prior to this win, was emotional and thanked his caddie for his support.

However, its place in boxing history will be determined by the events that transpire during the match in the MGM Grand Garden Arena. The article discusses a new mobile game called None*, which is a text-based riddle game distributed on iOS, Android, and Windows Phone devices. The app is intentionally mysterious, offering only one clue for each level and no supporting images, music, animations, or hints. The game consists of 50 levels in its first episode, with clues that start with simple math problems and evolve to name associations, random statements, and coordinates. The game's creator, Dimitris Chassapakis, suggests that once players complete the first 50 levels, they can subscribe for the release of Episode 2, yet a small percentage of players have managed to finish the app. Reviews are varied, with some finding it fun and satisfying, while others find it frustrating for its vague clues and lack of context.

The upcoming GCSE changes in foreign language education for 14-16 year olds aim to make learning more contemporary and engaging by incorporating relatable topics such as tattoos, music festivals, YouTube, and rap music. Teachers are being encouraged to abandon traditional topics like family or holidays and introduce modern content like reviewing foreign films, examining social media posts, and discussions on topics like online gaming, volunteering abroad, and foreign cuisine. The focus is on enhancing students' linguistic abilities and their overall enjoyment of the subject, which officials hope will increase engagement and language skills among students. The new approach, which involves a shift from memorizing themes to focusing on language building blocks, is also inspired by methods used to teach English as a foreign language.

A 21-year-old British woman named Danielle Davies gave birth to a 11lb 5oz baby named Harley after an eight-hour natural labor without any pain relief. The midwives were surprised due to the uncommon size, needing to weigh the baby numerous times for verification. Danielle, who previously had a 19-month-old daughter Layla, impressed hospital staff with her natural birth, despite having a blood clot on her brain detected a month before, which made her pregnancy and labor be induced. Danielle's pregnancy bump was notably larger compared to her first child. Senior midwife Jean Anderson, who has delivered babies up to 13lbs during her career, praised Danielle for her accomplishment.

The article discusses Linda and George Hunter, a couple who struggled to sell their home in Garrick Street, Liverpool, as the street underwent a regeneration scheme that led to neighboring houses being sold for £1. The Hunters, who became mortgage-free around 15 years ago and stayed put due to their elderly parents living nearby, felt their home was worth around £120,000. However, the council's offer of £85,000 was initially rejected. months later, the Hunters were told the offer had fallen through as their street was now part of Liverpool's 'Home for a Pound' scheme. The Hunters feel trapped and hope the council will reconsider the original offer, as they believe they have wasted their lives paying off a property now worth virtually nothing. The council believes the 'Home for a Pound' scheme will make the area more desirable and is in discussions with residents about their plan for regeneration.

Celebrities, such as Kim Kardashian, Mariah Carey, Amanda Holden, Myleene Klass, and Fearne Cotton, celebrated Easter by engaging in traditional activities like Easter egg hunts, making chocolate cupcakes, and decorating Easter baskets. Kim shared pictures of her decorating baskets for daughters North and niece and nephews. Mariah Carey made Easter cupcakes for her twins. Amanda Holden had an Easter egg hunt with her daughters. Myleene Klass had an egg hunt with her daughters in matching outfits. Fearne Cotton received beautiful Easter flowers from her mother-in-law. Other stars, like X Factor singer Sam Bailey and model Poppy Delevingne, also enjoyed their Easter celebrations.

A convicted fraudster, Gabrielle Yinka Saunders, stole £17,000 from her latest employer, Insight Investments, where she worked as a personal assistant. The stolen funds were used to pay for her £10,000 wedding, a £5,000 honeymoon in the Seychelles, and other personal expenses. Despite having been convicted of fraud twice previously, Saunders was spared jail and instead was sentenced to 15 months' imprisonment suspended for two years, with 200 hours of unpaid work, due to her repaying the money and her decision to retrain as a teacher.

A man, PJ Spraggins, lost 70lbs in a year to donate his kidney to his wife Tracy, who has been battling Lupus since childhood and was on the transplant list for seven years. However, his high blood pressure initially prevented the surgery. PJ then undertook a rigorous fitness regime, and after various tests, they eventually got the green light for the transplant in February 2015. Tracy, now recovering, has resumed her work as a special needs teacher, and the couple is grateful for the support from friends and well-wishers during their two-month recovery period.

An animal lover, Pauline Kidner, is nursing orphaned badger cubs back to health after they were found by dogs in separate incidents. One of the cubs, named Little Star, was rescued just in time as it was carried away by a Jack Russell. The cubs are now growing rapidly and have been introduced to a diet that includes custard creams. The goal is to release the cubs back into the wild once they are strong enough and have reduced human contact.

1. After struggling with Ferrari in 2014, Kimi Raikkonen is experiencing a resurgence this season, feeling confident that Ferrari could challenge for the Formula One world title.
2. Raikkonen recently finished fourth at the Chinese Grand Prix, just missing out on a podium place due to a late safety car, but believes Ferrari can consistently outperform their German rivals.
3. However, Raikkonen acknowledges he needs to improve in qualifying to have a better shot at the championship, as his mistake in qualifying for the Chinese Grand Prix placed him in a more difficult position for the race.

Rangers manager Stuart McCall is urging his team to end their poor away form and secure a crucial point against bottom side Dumbarton, as they aim to extend their second place position in the Championship. The match at the Bet Butler Stadium could potentially see Rangers open a four-point gap in second position.

Nigel Farage, the Ukip leader, argues in a debate at the European Parliament that allowing refugees into Europe could provide a cover for Islamic extremists, potentially leading to millions of people from North Africa being given passports that could allow them to move to Britain. Farage plans to use this issue as a focus in the election campaign, pointing out the potential risk of jihadis entering Europe and easily coming to the UK due to the open-borders policy. He considers this issue to be more significant than anything said by the party leaders about immigration during the campaign. This could be Farage's last speech in the European Parliament if he is elected as MP for Thanet South. On a separate campaign visit, he accused the SNP of being "openly racist."

1. Kai Windsor, initially born as a girl named Kaia, consistently displayed masculine preferences from a young age, such as favoring football over dolls and avoiding feminine attire. By the age of nine, Kai confided in his mother Rachel that he was, in fact, a boy.

2. As a result, Kai is scheduled to undergo hormone treatment to halt his puberty and prevent further development as a woman. Rachel, a single mother from Cheltenham, has been surprised but supportive, noting Kai's amazing school support and the remarkable improvement in his behavior and schoolwork after his transition.

3. The increased number of transgender referrals for children under 11 to the NHS indicates a growing issue, with families like the Windsors facing the challenges of gender identification and acceptance. Despite the difficulties, Rachel expresses gratitude for her son's newfound happiness and wellbeing.

A Hawaiian fisherman, Ron Ingraham, is missing again, just months after surviving 12 days lost at sea. In the previous incident, he was adrift for nearly two weeks, managing to radio for help and was eventually rescued. This time, his ship ran aground on rocks around a mile west of Hawaii's Lanai island. His sailing mate, Kenny Corder, was rescued but there's no sign of Ingraham. The Coast Guard is still searching for him. Ingraham's son, Zakary, was notified about his father's disappearance. The two had not spoken for more than 15 years but reunited after Ingraham's previous rescue.

A father and son, Nicholas Pence and David Pence, were shot dead in an execution-style murder in their home in Metairie, Louisiana, on Wednesday night after celebrating a victorious football game in their garage. The police arrested two individuals, Dexter Allen, 17, and Haraqyon Degruy, 18, in connection with the killings, but their relationship with the victims is unclear. The victims were found by David's wife, Nicholas's mother, who heard gunshots. The community is in mourning and shock, with the police investigating the incident as a potential botched burglary.

June Whitfield, known for her role as the eccentric grandmother in Absolutely Fabulous, is set to play Sister Ruth, a nun, in EastEnders. Her character will provide advice to Kat Moon (Jessie Wallace) as she struggles to cope with childhood sexual abuse. Whitfield stated that it was a delight to work with Wallace and valued EastEnders for the high standard of acting. Timothy West, a previous EastEnders cast member, had previously criticized the soap for not valuing older characters and actors.

1. Lewis Hamilton maintains his position as the wealthiest athlete in Britain with a fortune of £88million, according to the 2015 Sunday Times Sport Rich List. He is followed by Wayne Rooney, who observed an increment of £12million to £72million, propelling him to the second spot.

Researchers at Yahoo Labs have developed a sensor technology named Bodyprint, which can identify users based on the unique shape and size of various body parts, such as ears, palms, or fingers. This technology turns a standard touchscreen into a biometric scanner, eliminating the need for specialized hardware like fingerprint readers or infrared cameras. The goal is to make unlocking devices more convenient and accessible. Tests have shown a high level of accuracy, with 99.98% accuracy in classifying body parts and 99.52% accuracy in user identification. However, a release date for this technology in consumer devices has not been announced yet.

A woman named Belinda from Essex, UK, underwent a facelift in Turkey for a cheaper price, but it was botched, resulting in poorly done scars around her ears. The procedure left her with earlobes sewn to the side of her face. She now shares her regret and warns about the dangers of traveling abroad for cheap surgery. Belinda is scheduled to appear on TLC's Extreme Beauty Disasters to discuss her experience. A plastic surgeon, Vik Vijh, has accidentally inserted her scars in an incorrect position, pointing to potential risks like nerve damage and further scarring. After a corrective surgery by Mr. Vijh, Belinda is now happier and feels more confident.

In the article, Chuka Umunna, the shadow business secretary, accuses UKIP leader Nigel Farage of having a "problem with race," citing Farage's comments about "fully black" and "half black" UKIP supporters. This follows an incident where far-right supporters, including Gary Field, a former regional organizer for the English Defence League, were spotted campaigning for Farage in his South Thanet constituency. Umunna, whose father is Nigerian, criticizes UKIP for using "anti-immigration sentiment" and claims that the party harbors a "virus of racism." He asserts that UKIP dislikes modern Britain and fails to address racism within its ranks.

Model Maggie Rizer, 37, returned to her fit physique just nine weeks after giving birth to her third child, daughter Cecilia Kathryn. Despite facing praise for her quick recovery, Rizer, who is a fashion veteran, shared that she carefully chooses which images to post on her Instagram account. Her family, including husband Alex Mehran and sons Quinnlann Clancy (2) and Zander (3), are currently enjoying a family vacation at an unidentified tropical destination. Rizer initially gained fame as a supermodel in the late 90s and early 2000s but stopped modeling in 2004 after her stepfather gambled away her earnings, with losses estimated at over $7 million. Since then she has been a noted AIDS awareness activist.

Britons consume an average of four servings of cheese per week, with cheddar being the most popular variety. The survey also found that a significant number of cheese enthusiasts eat melted cheese with various items and pair it with pickles. A third of Brits enjoy a cheese sandwich when feeling hungry, and three in ten office workers eat cheese sandwiches daily. Another survey indicated that 32% of office workers eat an identical lunch daily for an average of 4.5 years, demonstrating a preference for repetition in meals. Food psychologist Greg Tucker suggests that while repetition provides comfort, trying new foods can be a source of excitement and motivation. Three recipes for alternative sandwich options are provided: chicken and mango sandwich with mint raita, smoked ham and egg with capers, gherkins, and mustard mayo, and feta with avocado and roasted red pepper.

A gray jacket and skirt dress worn by Vivien Leigh as Scarlett O'Hara in the 1939 film Gone With the Wind fetched $137,000 at auction. The dress, originally slate blue-gray, has faded to light gray from age, but was a key part of more than 150 items from the film offered by Heritage Auctions in Beverly Hills. The collection was previously owned by James Tumblin, who observed it on the floor at the Western Costume Company and purchased it for $20 in the 1960s. Other top-selling items included a straw hat worn by Leigh and a black bonnet worn by Olivia De Havilland as Melanie Wilkes.

A Turkish Airlines flight from Milan to Istanbul made an emergency landing at Ataturk Airport today due to an engine fire, marking the latest in a series of incidents involving the carrier. The fire was extinguished, and all 97 passengers were safely evacuated from the plane. The incident followed a recent incident on March 30 when another Turkish Airlines flight made an emergency landing after a 'bomb' note was found on board.

Adam Leheup, a 34-year-old architect, was acquitted of rape and sexual assault by a jury at Blackfriars Crown Court. During a night-long date, Leheup and the 25-year-old woman involved in the incident had consumed wine and cocktails, with the woman allowing Leheup to remove her bra and massage her back with oil. Although the woman alleged that Leheup ignored her cries of "no" and forced himself on her, the jury found him not guilty after a week-long trial. Leheup had been communicating with 35 women online at the time, regularly having sex with six of them, but had stopped short with the complainant. The incident occurred after the pair had used the mobile app "Let's Date" to meet on July 9, 2013.

AleXsandro Palombo, an Italian artist, launched the #briefmessage campaign, encouraging women to write thoughts on gender violence on their underwear and share them via social media. His goal is to challenge machismo and promote education about gender violence. The responses have been diverse and powerful, with messages ranging from cheeky statements to defense against domestic violence. Many men have also participated, expressing support for the campaign. Palombo is known for creating art that addresses controversial social issues.

Nick Clegg faced protests over his broken tuition fees pledge in Surbiton, South West London, where he also criticized George Osborne's "dangerous" economic plan. Clegg labeled Osborne as a "very dangerous man" and accused him of wanting to make drastic cuts that would harm public services. In contrast, Clegg described David Cameron as a "classic traditional shire Tory," whom he could tolerate. The Lib Dem leader stressed the need to prevent Osborne's proposed cuts and challenge the Labour Party's approach to public spending. Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Danny Alexander claimed that a senior Tory had told him in a private meeting that the Conservatives would prioritize tax cuts for the affluent while leaving working-class people to the Lib Dems.

Sharon Edwards, a 55-year-old teacher, has been missing since March 14 in Grafton, NSW. Her family is struggling to come to terms with her disappearance as her car was found in the driveway and her clothes were in the washing basket, but there's no sign of forced entry or missed bank or social media activity. Police are treating the investigation as a homicide due to a lack of history of mental illness, but Edwards has no known enemies. The family, including her husband and three sons, have made an emotional appeal for information. Edwards was last seen spending the afternoon with friends at a hotel and was due to travel to Brisbane to help care for her granddaughter. Strike Force Burrow is investigating the circumstances of her disappearance. Anyone with information about her whereabouts is urged to contact Grafton Police Station or Crime Stoppers.

The husband, Steven Nelms, authored a heartfelt essay praising his stay-at-home wife Glorianna, detailing the monetary value of her various contributions to their family, including childcare, cooking, housekeeping, and grocery shopping. He admitted feeling ashamed for not showing adequate appreciation for his wife's efforts and realized he couldn't afford for her to be a full-time homemaker, estimating her worth to be nearly double his actual income. Prime Minister David Cameron is facing criticism for his election campaign's lackluster message and failure to pull ahead in the polls, prompting him to vow to continue focusing on economic issues like jobs, business, and childcare. Despite speculation about a potential coup against him, led by Boris Johnson, and criticism from high-profile Tory donors for a perceived lack of energy and vision, Cameron insists he will emphatically focus on the economy and jobs as key issues in the election. Two former police officials, Trish Cohen (former police chief) and Rich Medley (former assistant police chief), quit their jobs in Parma, Missouri, following the election of Tyus Byrd, a black woman, as mayor. Cohen and Medley allege that their home addresses were shared online by Byrd's family members, and they feared for their safety. Byrd, however, denies knowing the reasons for the city employees' departure and maintains that race played no role in the issue. Cohen and Medley claim they were not informed about their jobs' security, while Byrd denies ever threatening to fire officers or interfere with police matters. Both women did not respond to requests for comment.

Photographer Johan Bavman, a father living in Sweden, which is known for offering generous parental leave, decided to document the real-life experiences of other fathers taking advantage of the program. He found a series of fathers using their "daddy months" or "partner months," as mandated by Sweden, and captured their devotion, tiredness, and bonding with their children through photography. These fathers have become more understanding of their wives and even their own mothers, and some are considering a career change to accommodate their parenthood. Bavman aims to photograph 60 such fathers for an exhibition and book.

In Arizona, twins Eli and Silas Keslar, aged 18 months, drowned in a canal after their mother observed a bee and lost grip of their stroller. The mother, Alexis Keslar, attempted to rescue her sons but was unable to due to the steep and challenging banks of the canal. The tragedy has prompted authorities to issue warnings about the potential danger of canals that may appear harmless. A GoFundMe page has been set up to cover memorial and medical costs for the parents, Mark and Alexis Keslar.

Eden Hazard, Chelsea's standout player of the season, demonstrated his growth and importance in the team's imminent title victory by scoring the decisive goal in a 1-0 win over Manchester United on Saturday. Manager Jose Mourinho has praises Hazard's defensive work and his consistent performance even when the team isn't at its best. A mother, Latisha Fisher, has been charged with second-degree murder for allegedly smothering her 20-month-old son, Gavriel Ortiz-Fisher, in a bathroom at a Manhattan restaurant, claiming she did so to protect him from being eaten. Fisher has a history of psychiatric problems, including a previous diagnosis of schizophrenia, and was evaluated as mentally fit as recently as last year. The Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens panel at Anaheim Convention Center was attended by Carrie Fisher (Princess Leia) and Mark Hamill (Luke Skywalker), with Harrison Ford (Han Solo) absent due to recovery from a plane crash. Bill Nye, also known as "the Science Guy", joined President Barack Obama on Earth Day for a visit to the Florida Everglades, during which they traveled aboard Air Force One. Notably, Nye shared with press that he loves the smell of jet fuel before the flight. The trip was intended to promote the administration's efforts to reduce carbon pollution and preserve wetlands, including the Everglades. However, some pointed out the potential irony of jet travel contributing to carbon emissions while advocating for climate change action.

Floyd Mayweather Jr. reminisced about his friends' reactions when he announced his intention to become an independent boxing businessman, stating they called him crazy. He broke away from promoter Bob Arum and will face Manny Pacquiao in Las Vegas on May 2, both earning over $100 million. Mayweather takes pride in being his own boss for this historic fight, which critics argue is five years too late. The media and fans gathered at Mayweather's gym for a workout, with security guards present due to the event's significance to Las Vegas' economy. He acknowledges the MGM Grand Garden as his venue of choice, citing the gift of a luxury watch from them five years ago. Elderflower Fields, a family-oriented festival hosting a diverse range of activities in an idyllic setting, is geared towards providing children and families with an immersive and enriching experience in sports, music, arts, environment, and food. The festival offers free activities for children, including instrument try-outs, music workshops, sports camps, rafting, and orienteering. It also features professional performances, such as by Danny and the Champions Of The World, Patch and The Giant, and The Kings Parade. Chelsea has won six spots in the Professional Footballers' Association Premier League Team of the Year. The defense includes John Terry, Gary Cahill, Branislav Ivanovic, and Ryan Bertrand, with Ivanovic and Cahill both considered for transfer to other teams. Eden Hazard and Nemanja Matic, both from Chelsea, along with Philippe Coutinho from Liverpool and Alexis Sanchez from Arsenal, were in midfield. Harry Kane from Tottenham and Diego Costa from Chelsea are the forwards. Fans may feel disappointed that Cesc Fabregas, who has made 16 league assists, was not included. Michael Owen, a 21-year-old father, was tragically killed in a car accident in Crowborough, East Sussex, while preparing for his daughter's fifth birthday. He had recently received a job offer in window screen repair. Kyle Careford, the other occupant of the car, is thought to have died just before his 21st birthday. The men were friends and local residents, and their loss has been mourned by family, friends, and community members. The accident occurred when the car they were in lost control, crashing into a church wall and overturning. Police and emergency services are investigating the cause of the collision.

2. Manager Manuel Pellegrini's position at Manchester City is under scrutiny after a series of losses, including a 4-1 defeat to their rivals, and critics argue that his calm demeanor is ill-suited for galvanizing the team during tough times.
